January. 1997 for setting up of Galvanizing Complex in Assam at an esti mated cost of Rs. 42.85 
crore with a completion schedule of 24 months. The initial techno-economic viability of the 
project was worked out assuming that the project wou ld be financed by internal resources of 
SAIL and commercial borrowings\\ ith the debt-equity or ratio of I: I at an estimated project cost 
of Rs. 42 .85 crore (fourth Qtr/96).Due to SAIL's difficult liquidity position. the enti re expenditure 
of Rs. 12.51 crore made on the project so far has been funded through commercial borrowings. 
The viabi lity of the project was reassessed by M/s IFCI Financial Service Ltd. ,who have 
indicated that under the present funding pattern. the project does not appear to be financially 
\ iable. The) suggested that SAIL should obtain funds from external sources in the form of 
capital in,estment subsid} /grant. Matter was taken up v. ith the Planning Commission to 
consider release of Rs. 25 crore to SAIL as an investme nt subs idy for the project from the "No n­
Lapsable Central Pool of Resources" (NLCP R) meant for North Eastern Regio n in order to 
salvage the project. Planning Commission, after examining the project have concluded that its 
techno-eco nomic viability is doubtful, and therefore the project is not suitable for support from 
NLCPR. SA IL Board has decided to keep the project in abeyance at the present and devise 
alternative strateg ies. including identificati on of suitable party who may be interested in owning 
and executing the project. In pursuance of same, SAIL has appointe d M /s PNB Capital Services 
Ltd. as its Strategic Advisor to locate a suitable joint venture partner /o utright purchaser for the 
project. MIS PN B Capital Services had invited bids from the three short listed bidders . Only one

approach towards development of North Eastern region . On the one hand the Ministry got 
e:-..emption from the Planning Commission for spending I 0% of gross budgetary support for

GENERAL OBSERVATIONS / RECOMMENDATIONS 
23. Tax proposal affecting Steel Industry 
23.1 Reacting on the existing tax-structure the Ministry of Steel stated that the existing tax 
structu re is quite progressive and reasonable for the growt h of the steel indu stry .Over the years 
the gove rnment has reduced the import duties on raw materials for stee l industry and have 
removed anomalies existing in the tax structure. The Ministry of Stee l viewed that there are 
certai n issues i.e. Reduction in import duty on non coking coal from 25% to 5% at par wit h 
coking coa l ;Reduc tion in import duty on metallurgical coke from 15% to 5%.; Reduction in 
import duty on some of the raw materials for refractory making; Reduction in import duty on low 
silica limestone. zinc and graphite electrodes which are inputs for steel making and Reduction in 
excise duty on l ong products like GP/GC sheets which are used for rural housing which need to 
be addressed. 
23 .. 2 The Committee is pleased to note that the existing tax struct ure is progressive and 
reasonable for the growth of steel industry . The Committee hopes that the Ministry of 
Steel wou ld take up the remaining anomalies in the existing tax-structure affect ing the 
general prospects of stee l industry . 
24. Problems in Exports and Imports 
24.1 The Secretary, during the course of his oral evidence, informed the Committee " unless and 
until, we have export market for ourselves, our industry will not be able to sustain for itself. We 
have been able to export 3 million tonnes in a year. But, in the recent past, countries like the U.S. 
and Europe have imposed anti-dump ing duties. On the one hand, the U.S. talks about WTO 
compatibi lity, and whenever India takes any act ion to safeguard its industry, they say that it 
should be done as per the provisions of the WTO; whereas, on the ot her hand, in their own 
country, they are placing all sorts of restrictions and imposing very high duties the Secretary 
s~ated. He further stated that recently, in the Clinton regime, they passed an Act which provides 
that the revenue collected by way of anti-dumping duties could be passed on to the steel units. 
S:>, it is essential for us to keep our foothold in the internati onal market , the Secretary felt. 
Another problem is imports in the form of inflow of seconds and defectives at a very cheap rate 
the Secretary informed. That is also harming the domestic steel industry. The Ministry of Steel 
have taken up the matter with the Ministry of Commerce, and after a great deal of persuasion , the 
Ministry of Comme rce have agreed to impose some sort of non-tariff barriers, at least, for 
stconds and defectives, the Secretary added. 
24.2 The Comm ittee understand that exports are essential ingredieht of the growth of industry. 
Similarly, imports should not ca use glaring damag e to the indigenous industry. The Committee 
therefore recommends that Ministry of Commerce may take necessary steps to find solution, to 
the problems of our steel industry faced in internati ona l market in respect of exports and from the 
imports. Ministry of Steel may pursue the matter with Ministry of Com merce. 
25. Railway Freight 
25.1 The Secretary informed the Comm ittee that because of the two percent increase in the freight 
in the Railway Budget of 2001-2002 they have been adversely affected. In fact, it is only the 
public sector companies like SAIL and RINL which are using rail for transporting their finished 
products. The new steel plants are using road traffic for transporting their finished products. 

Even this two per cent hike in freight is going to cost the SAIL about Rs. 28 crores more and to 
RINL about Rs. I 0 crores more, the Secretary added. 
25.2. The Secretary also informed that another problem with the Railways is relating to 
transport of iron-ore from Bailadila to Vizag. When that railway line was constructed, the 
Railways incurred a lot of expenditure on constructing that line. At that time, it was decided to 
levy some additional freight on transportation of iron-ore. The additional freight was charged for 
the entire sector. It was also decided at that time that when the traffic would reach the level of 60 
lakh tonnes per annum, that additional freight would be withdrawn . Today, the traffic has 
reached to 120 lakh tonnes per annum. But it is still continuing. The Secretary also stated that 
they have taken up this issue with the Ministry of Railways and there is a strong case for 
withdrawal on this surcharge. 
25.3 The Committee understands that the two percent hike in railway freight would have a 
severe impact on SAIL and RINL. Ministry of Steel may take up the matter with Railways. The 
Committee also feels that the additional freight charged on transportation of iron ore from 
Baladila to Vizag should have been stopped after it reached the level of 60 lakh tonnes per annum 
as per the decision taken at that time. Now, it has reached 120 lakh tonnes. The Committee 
recommends that the Ministry of Steel may pursue the matter with Railways and Railways also 
may consider removing this at the earliest. 
26. Anti Dumping 
26.1 The Secretary Ministry of Steel during the course of oral evidence stated ,"the USA has 
the largest market for our exports. The anti dumping duty is against a company specific and 
product specific . But, there is a legal battle. In some cases, we have won and in some cases we 
have lost. Suppose, some company is exporting against contract in USA. The moment anti­
dumping duty is imposed, that schedule is affected for next six months . What happens in USA is 
that they first impose preliminary determination in very large number of cases, and just on first 
hearing, they see what is the preliminary case and they impose a duty of 40-45% . Generally , 
after hearing both the parties 50% of case are disposed of in this way an early stage. 
Whether the duty is conformed or it is not confirmed , is decided later . When the Committee 
sought to know as to why this cannot be done in India, he informed the Committee they ," we 
have made a request before the Ministry of Commerce.... We want some amendment to the 
procedures. We have already requested the Ministry that provisional duties must be imposed ". 
26.2 The Committee observes with concern that the anti-dumping system that is prevailing in 
other countries is different from that of ours. In the anti-dumping system of our country, 
complaints are received and after examination of those complaints , the witnes ses are called . Then 
the whole thing is enquired upon and it takes a long time, may be one year or six months. Later 
on, the decision is taken. During this period of complaint and inquiry, the materials will 
automatically be coming into the country. Then after one year, if it is found that this import was 
not required, then imposition of certain restrictions is resorted to. But by that time, the damage 
would have taken place to the industry or to the trade . The Committee feels that the time has 
come for our country to think and act on it seriously. The Committee recommends that our anti­
dumping law also may be brought at par with that of other countries, particularly America.

required for financially weak/loss-making PSUs and Government should allocate higher budgetary 
support to such loss making PSUs, enabling them to meet revenue as well as capital expenditure. In 
this regard, the Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should continue to assess the 
financial requirement of each steel PSU and take up the matter with the Ministry of Finance and the 
Planning Commission in the right earnest for higher allocation. In case the PSUs are not able,to raise

RECOMMENDATION NO. 4-5
 
4.         The Sub-Committee feels that recovery of pending cases should be expedited by fixing accountability at district
administration level also.  In addition the record of pending cases be computerised and updated at regular intervals.  There
should be time bound specific targets to be monitored at District level by District magistrates.
 
5.         The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government to explore ways and means for recovery of PMRY loans
under defaults, as delays occur in serving of notices and appearance in the Court.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The Office has been monitoring to improve/expedite the recovery of loan dues under the PMRY.  The State/UTs
have been requested to include in their existing Land Revenue Arrears Recovery Acts, recovery of loan arrears under
PMRY, so that these are recoverable as arrears of land revenue.  The State/UTs were requested to conduct joint recovery
drives.  A letter was written to State/UTs on 26.6.2000 reiterating the need to take necessary steps to improve recovery of
loan under the scheme.  A copy of the letter written to State/UTs on 26.6.2000 is enclosed for ready reference (Annexure
– III).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.  6             
 
The Sub-Committee observes that bankers generally raise their concern about the late communication of targets to
them from the Government.  For example, targets are being communicated in August/September wherein they are to be
achievable by March (end of financial year).  The Sub-Committee recommends that the targets for PMRY should be
communicated to Banks from the Government, well in time to avoid any kind of time constraint.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The basic target for the year 2000-2001 under the PMRY were communicated to State/UTs and to the RBI on
19.4.2000.  The additional targets under the scheme were communicated to the State/UTs and to the RBI on 16.6.2000. 
The RBI has been requested to convey the bank-wise target as early as possible in the light of the recommendation of the

Committee.  A copy of the letter written to the RBI in this regard is enclosed. (Annexure – II).
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO. 7 & 11
 
7.         The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government that DICs should avoid disproportionate sponsoring of
applications under PMRY.  This act, in return, will minimise the pendency rate of applications.
 
11.       The Sub-Committee has noticed that DICs fail to complete the identification process well in advance.  As a matter
of fact, in place of transmission of applications to banks under PMRY, in a phased manner, they do the same in bunching.
 
The Sub-Committee, therefore, recommends that it has to be ensured that the flow of applications from DICs to
banks; take place in a phased manner and the practice of bunching of applications should be stopped.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The Office of the Dev. Commissioner(SSI), while communicating the annual target to the State/UTs prescribes a
quarterly schedule for sponsoring of applications by the District Task force Committees to banks.  A copy of the schedule
is enclosed for ready reference (Annexure – IV).  The State/UTs have been requested to issue necessary instructions to the
DICs to adhere to the schedule prescribed for sponsoring of applications to avoid disproportionate sponsoring of
applications to banks to avoid bunching of applications at the fag end of the year.  A copy of the letter issued to State/UTs
is enclosed. (Annexure – V)
 
 
RECOMMENDATION/ OBSERVATION NO. 8
 
The Sub-Committee observes that under PMRY, quality applications are not being sponsored to   banks.  As
regards this shortcoming, the Sub-Committee feels that Branch Managers should be involved actively in selecting the
beneficiaries and the activities.
           
ACTION TAKEN
 
The guidelines of the PMRY scheme provides for the inclusion of the lead bank and other participating banks as
the members of the district task force committees.  The subsequent guidelines also provide that all participating banks in a
district may participate in the district task force committee meetings on a rotational basis.  A copy of the letter is enclosed
(Annexure – VI).  The RBI vide Circular dated 19.11.96 has instructed to CMDs of all Indian Scheduled Commercial
Banks that banks can receive the applications directly and send them to the sponsoring agencies with their observations on
the viability and bankability of the project.  A copy of the letter is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure – VII)
 
            The RBI has been requested to reiterate the necessary instructions in view of the recommendation of the
Committee.

As per the provisions made under PMRY, loans should be in the ratio of 50%, 30% and 20% in respect  of
industry, services and business sector.  During the course of the discussion, the Sub-Committee came to know that mostly
applications are received for business activities and applications regarding industry are few in numbers.  The Sub-
Committee feels that steps should be taken to ensure that the ratio of loans for all three activities are maintained according
to provisions contained in the Scheme.
 
 
 
ACTION TAKEN

The Sub-Committee notes with discontent that till now banks are not very enthusiastic about projects under

Boards can prepare their action plan in accordance with the guidelines of the KVIC.  The Sub-Committee also views that
there is necessity to ensure the confidence of entrepreneurs about the continuation of the programme and easy availability
of funds.

Regarding Margin Money Scheme, the RBI has already provided necessary code Numbers to Village Industries

and Margin Money Scheme which will enables the Banks to incorporate necessary provision for this scheme in the
District Credit Plans at appropriate stage.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 35
 
The Sub-Committee came to know that Khadi sector has been providing more employment opportunities
especially for the women folk in rural areas.  Some of the State Governments have been providing incentive wages for
spinners and weavers.  The Sub-Committee thus feels that Central Government should also provide such wage incentives
in order to retain and improve the employment opportunities in Khadi sector.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The wage rate/incentive of Khadi Sector is regulated by the provision made in the Khadi cost chart.
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS NO. 45
 
The Sub-Committee came to know that usual annual average stock holding of coir products is of Rs. 15 Crore. The
Sub-Committee feels that adequate measures should be taken by Government to clear the stock holding of coir products.
 
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
The measures taken for domestic market development and export promotion are expected to increase the demand
for coir and coir and coir products.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH REPLIES OF THE GOVERNMENT
HAVE NOT BEEN ACCPETED BY THE COMMITTEE
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 2
 
The Sub-Committee notes that under PMRY, there is subsidy ceiling of Rs.7,500/.  The Sub-Committee is of the
view that the practice of subsidy ceiling may be dispensed with and instead 15 per cent subsidy may be made, admissible
for all quantum of loan amount.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The rate of subsidy has since been revised for the NE States.  It is @ 15 per cent of the project cost subject to a
ceiling of Rs.15,000/- per beneficiary.  It has been decided in the 10
th Meeting of High powered Committee for PMRY
that the ceiling on subsidy may also be raised for weaker sections i.e. SC/STs, ex-servicemen, physically disabled persons
and women and also for the States/UTs of J&K, Sikkim, Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Lakshadweep.  This could be
implemented only after approval from the Cabinet.
 
COMMENTS OF THE COMMITTEE
 
The Committee  hopes  that   approval of Cabinet  would  be obtained  at the earliest and it would be implemented
expeditiously.
 
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION NO.3
 
The Sub-Committee observes that the recovery under PMRY is far from satisfaction.  The Sub-Committee,
accordingly, is of the view that the recovery process of PMRY loans at bank level can be strengthened by creating District

level Recovery cells with every bank.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The RBI has been requested to initiate necessary action on the recommendations of the Committee.  A copy of the
communication sent to RBI is enclosed.  (Annexure – II). 
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
The Committee recommends that the Government may pursue the matter with RBI for an early implementation of
the recommendation.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.  10
 
The general view is that viability aspects of proposals are ignored by DICs while sponsoring the  applications
under PMRY.  The Sub-Committee recommends that DICs should go thoroughly into the details of each and every
proposal including spot verification, technical feasibility and financial viability.
In this connection, the Sub-Committee further recommends that the plea of helplessness from DICs, for want of
staff should not be taken as an excuse.
 
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The issue was discussed in the 10
th Meeting of the High powered Committee for the PMRY held on 22.3.2000 
and it was decided that State/UTs may be requested to instruct to the DICs to identify viable projects in their respective
districts and prepare project profiles for the guidelines of the prospective entrepreneurs under the PMRY.  In addition
project profiles prepared by the SISIs used by various financial institutions (FIs) and similar agencies can also utilised.  A
copy of the letter written to all State/UTs is enclosed for ready reference. (Annexure – VIII).
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            The Committee feels that DICs will have to play a pro-active role. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
recommendation that DICs should go thoroughly into every proposal. DICs  should invariably prepare project profiles for
assistance of  prospective entrepreneurs.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 15
 
The Sub-Committee strongly recommends that necessary steps should be taken by the bank management to do
away with the prevailing psychosis of bank branches that if they start sanctioning the cases of PMRY on regular basis then
pending cases of non-performing banks will be thrust upon them.
 
ACTION TAKEN
 
            The finding of the committee has been communicated to the RBI.  A copy of the letter written to RBI is enclosed
for ready reference. (Annexure – II)
 
COMMENTS/OBSERVATION  OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            The Committee feels that RBI needs to do a thorough review of the system.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 16  &  17
 
16.       The Sub-Committee strongly recommends that RBI’s guidelines for disposing of applications under PMRY within
the time-period of thirty days must be adhered to by banks.  Concerning it, the responsibilities should be fixed to
undertake needful corrective measures.

17.       The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government to take suitable steps to minimise the rejection ratio by banks

has issued instructions, implementation  should be regularly reviewed and monitored.

banks differ on ISES issued by the KVIC.  The Sub-Committee recommends that government should take necessary

sector under the Chairmanship of Shri S. K. Kalia, the then Managing Director of NABARD in 1993, was taken into

th July, 1994 (copy enclosed).  Annexure XII.

            The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation in this regard and feels that RBI should regularly monitor this

The Sub-Committee recommends that necessary initiatives should be taken, so that NABARD’S  participation in
KVIC’s Margin Money Scheme enhances particularly for NABARD’S refinance facility for the purpose.

The KVIC regularly inter-acts with the NABARD on various issues, where NABARD can give

            The  Committee  is   of the view that  enhancement of  NABARD’s  participation in KVIC’s Margin Money
Scheme in respect of refinance facility   should   be  ensured .

Over a period of time, more than 25% of the Khadi units have become sick due to various reasons.  There is no
programme with the KVIC for rehabilitating the sick units.  The Sub-Committee thus recommends that revival of sick
units should become a continuous programme alongwith the establishment of new units.  Moreover, the continuous
monitoring of the functioning of the old units will ensure the recovery of dues and continuous employment in rural areas.

The KVIC has already formulated guidelines for revitalizing sick Khadi institutions (copy enclosed) Annexure

The guidelines may be implemented at the earliest. Implementation of  guidelines for  revitalizing  sick khadi
institutions  should be monitored   properly .   The Committee   reiterates  the recommendation that revival    of sick units

The Sub-Committee came to know that KVIBs have been implementing Margin Money Scheme of the KVIC,
wherein the scheme envisages loan portion of the project cost to be met from Consortium Bank  Credit (CBC) sources and
margin money from the KVIB budgetary sources.  The Sub-Committee recommends that KVIBs should be better
equipped and strengthened so that they can become the catalysts of rural industries in the country.

The KVIC impress upon the State Governments to strengthen the infrastructure facilities of State KVI Boards so

In order to implement the REGP/Margin Money Scheme, the KVIC had also placed Margin Money Grant with
State/UT KVI Boards in advance, so that the programme can be implemented without any delay.  However, it is observed
that due to weak infrastructure facilities some of the State/UT KVI Boards are not in a position to utilise such grants made
available to them even after a lapse of considerable time.  As far as projects under Margin Money Scheme are concerned,
the State/UT KVI Boards are empowered to recommend projects by ensuring its techno-economic viability without
awaiting for the prior approval from the KVIC.
 
 
COMMENT/OBSERVATION OF THE COMMITTEE
 
            It is unfortunate that funds are not being utilized  due to  lack  of infrastructure facilities. Central Govt. should take
up the matter with all state/UT Govts. for improving infrastructure facilities.

The Sub-Committee impresses upon the Government that more importance should be given for marketing of the
goods produced by KVI sector.  This will facilitate the expansion of rural industries by providing linkages.

other commercial  organizations  to promote  goods  in the market    and earn recognition.    The Committee reiterates  its
earlier recommendation in this regard. Better marketing strategies are required to be adopted.   
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.42
 
            The Sub-Committee came to know that existing Co-operativisation Scheme was approved in the Eight Plan period.
The quantum of assistance allotted for managerial subsidy is not enough to appoint managerial personnel in the societies.

REPORT

1.         Brief   Background

east coast. Nalco operates   bauxite mines  at panchpatmali in district Koraput (Orissa).  It runs a  0.8  million tonnes per
Annum  alumina refinery at   Damanjodi in Koraput  District, and  230000  tonnes per  Annum  Aluminium   Smelter  at
Angul  in Orissa.  The authorised capital of the company  has been reduced    from Rs. 1288.62  crores to  Rs.644.31
crores after the approval  of the  Cabinet.   The Government of India  holds  87.15% of equity  in Nalco, the balance
12.85%  being  held by financial institutions, employees, public etc.Nalco is a zero debt company  and  has been granted
Miniratna status by Government of India and it has also been  classified  as a    star  trading house. Nalco  exports 
Alumina  & Aluminium to  over thirty countries.  It has been  accorded ISO  9002 & ISO  14001 certification.

Expansion programme of  NALCO
Nalco  has undertaken   a  massive   expansion programme of   Rs.3700 crores  of  its       bauxite mines, alumina
refinery, smelter, captive power plant and port facilities.  The resources for the entire  expansion programme  are to be
internally generated.
This includes expansion    of  the capacity of  bauxite mines  from 2.4 millions tonnes  per year  to 4.8 million tonnes 
per year and that of  Alumina Refinery from 0.8  million tonnes  per year  to 1.575 million tonnes per year   at an 
investment  of Rs.1664.60 crores.    The project   was to be implemented within 51 months from the date of government
approval i.e. 18.12.1996.
The Government also approved   expansion of capacity of  Aluminium Smelter and Captive Power Plant of Nalco at 
Angul   so as to  increase the capacity of the Smelter from  230000 TPY  to 345000 TPY  and  that  of the  captive
power plant from the existing  720 MW   to  840 MW at an  investment of Rs.2062 crores .  The project  was also to be
implemented in  51 months from  the date of  Government approval i.e. 3
rd February 1998.

4.1       The Committee visited the Nalco’s port facilities at Visakhapatnam  on 20
th January, 2001.        The Committee
took a tour of the entire facility through sea .  This port facility is             located             on 9.14 hectares  and caters to
import of 1.2 lakh tonnes of Caustic Soda and   exports of 3.75 lakh tonnes of calcined alumina.  In addition it also
handles export of Aluminium    Metal by containers/barges and also imports  materials through Visakhapatnam Port.   
Nalco has  obtained on lease an additional 1.424 hectares of land   from Visakhapatnam     Port for expansion purpose.
After completion of the ongoing         expansion, the unit would be able to handle 11.25 lakh tonnes of Alumina and 2.4
lakh             tonnes of Caustic Soda. The Committee was informed that expansion work is in progress          for
increasing the capacity of Alumina handling facilities from 3.75 lakh tonnes to 11.25 lakhs tonnes per year and           
Caustic Soda handling facilities from 1.2 lakh tonnes to           2.4 lakh tonnes. However the    existing caustic soda
facilities would cater to the        increased capacity. The expansion work            under progress is for Alumina handling
only.      The Committee was also informed that the Expansion work consists of the following:-
Wagon unloading system of 1100MT per hour capacity
One additional storage alumina silo of 25000 tonnes capacity
Additional Railway tracks of 1.6 Kms.
the consultancy and project supervision has been given to MECON Ltd.
the entire project cost is 36.37 crores.
The Committee observed that the progress of the Civil and Piling work and enabling work on expansion of port

TPY is being done in two stages. The first stage of expansion, known as De-bottlenecking got completed in May 2000.
This has raised the capacity of the Refinery to 1.05 Million TPY from the existing 0.8 Million TPY. The installation of
third stream of Alumina Refinery i.e. expansion from 1.05 Million TPY to 1.575 Million TPY, is expected to be
completed by 30
th September, 2001 as against the scheduled date of March,2001.  Based on the present status of the
project.  The total cost is expected to be much below the approved cost of Rs 1664.60 crores. It is expected that there
will be a saving of about Rs.300 crores on this project The Committee was informed that as against the total project cost
of Rs.1664.60 crores, the cumulative commitment made upto Dec’2000 is about Rs.1302 crores. The Committee was
further informed that the total project was to be entirely financed from internal resources.
In response to the  Committees  query   about the techno-economic viability of the expansion projects of the Bauxite
mines from 2.4 millions tons per year(MTPY) to 4.8 MTPY and that of the Alumina Refinery from 0.8 MTPY to 1.575
MTPY at an investment of Rs.1664.60 crore the Committee was informed that  the approval for M&R expansion project
was based on the techno-economic viability of the project at June 1996 price level with a post tax IRR of 14.64%.The
impact of this expansion on the overall financial performance of the company will be good and will result in higher
profits.
The Committee is not happy to note that the installation of third steam of      Alumina Refinery is getting delayed. All
efforts need to be taken for early     installation.
The Committee also observed the progress of the expansion work on the Nalco’s captive power plant during its visit to
Angul on 23 rd January 2001. The Committee was informed that  the captive power plant capacity is being increased
from 720 MW to 840 MW. This project envisages an investment of Rs 2062 crores and is scheduled to be completed by
May 2002.  The Committee was informed that a proposal to further enhance the capacity of the unit VIII  of CPP from
840 MW to 960 MW with an additional  estimated cost of Rs.480 crores was under consideration of the government.
However it may be  mentioned that the government has approved the proposal on 14.2.2001 and the project is expected
to be completed in 36 months.
The Committee was pleased to note that Nalco has one of the best captive power plants in the country with the cost of
production of power per unit being one of the lowest. The Committee noted that the power plant was a major factor in
providing intrinsic strength to Nalco and one of the main reasons for Nalco being able to keep its cost of production of
alumina competitive. The Committee also noted that Nalco would be having a large surplus  power after its expansion.
The Committee therefore recommends that Nalco should explore possibilities of commercial sale of surplus power at
competitive prices. Efforts may be made to complete the project in time as per the schedule.
The Committee was informed  that after implementation of the Expansion Project of Smelter, Nalco will be the largest
single Aluminum Producer in India. Further Nalco’s enlistment with LME will also help in expanding Nalco’s
international presence. The present trend of metal prices also suggests that the expansion project will help  in achieving  
higher profitability and competitive edge. The Committee hopes that NALCO would achieve higher profitability after
expansion and reap rich benefits from it.
6.    Financial restructuring
During  the course of discussions at Bhubhaneswar,    the Committee    asked  CMD, Nalco  about the    the     reasons 
for reducing the   paid up   share capital of Nalco to 50%  from Rs.1288.62           crore to 644.31 crore in  the year
1998.  The Committee also  asked  about the   impact of  such  capital restructuring   on the  physical and financial
performance of the company.  The CMD of Nalco  informed    that   relative to  (a) Sales turnover, (b) Profits after  tax
and (c) Financial ratios including  paid up capital of competitors like  Hindalco and Indal, the paid up share capital   of 
Rs.1288.62 crore of Nalco  was considered very much on the higher side and  hence the stock          performance ratios
like EPS, PE multiple and Share price etc. were   low  and  was not adequately  reflecting the  intrinsic   strength   of
Nalco. Hence, capital restructuring  was done with the prior permission of the government. Accordingly 50% of paid up
equity capital of 1288.62% was converted to redeemable secured debentures. The paid up equity capital after
restructuring was 644.31 crores out of which Govt of India holding is Rs.561.50 crores(87.15%).  The Committee was
also informed that the original project cost was partly financed by external commercial borrowings and partly by equity
subscribed by govt. of India. The entire foreign currency loan has been repaid by 30.09.98  and Nalco has become a zero
debt company except for debt created out of equity capital through a scheme of capital restructuring with the prior

Public Sector Undertaking in terms of excellent financial parameters. The Committee during the course of discussions

7.    Technical know-how
The Committee  was informed       that Aluminium   Pechiney  of France,  a  world   leader in Aluminium  technology,
have supplied  Nalco  the  know how  and the basic engineering technology for  Alumina  and Aluminium Plant.  The
Committee was further informed that there are    many plants  world wide working  with  their technology.  M/s
Engineers India Limited(EIL) were the prime Indian consultants for Mines, Alumina Refinery and Aluminium smelter.
They have also been engaged for the ongoing expansion projects of Bauxite mine, Alumina refinery and smelter plants.
M/s Development Consultants Ltd(DCL) were the consultants for the captive power plant and steam generation plant
and M/s Howe India (P) ltd for the Port facilities. M/s Dasturco have been appointed as consultant for expansion of
Captive Power Plant and M/s. MECON for expansion of Port facilities. The Committee was  apprised that the  quality
of   Alumina and  Aluminium produced  by Nalco meets all international  quality   standards  because of its technology. 
The  cost   of production of  Alumina  of  Nalco is lowest in the world because of appropriate technology and logistics.
Hence Nalco will be in a position to compete in the international market for its quality with cost economics.
It is good to obtain outside technology whenever required. The Committee recommends that Nalco should have a
strong  R&D set up and wherever possible in-house expertise should be utilized instead of always depending on outside
agencies.
8.    Capacity utilization of captive Power Plant
The Committee  was informed that  the captive  power plant is capable  of supplying power  to the Smelter. However,
the power system is connected to Orissa grid, which is unreliable and unstable.   The voltage and frequency variations
are high and at times the  system trips   due to external   fault, causing a total black out of the grid This was  a  frequent
phenomenon earlier .  The situation   at present is  better after NTPC super thermal power plant  came into existence.
The Committee was further  informed that    frequent   power interruption  has detrimental effect on pot operation.  In
1998, the pot  line,  handling of metal at cast house, power failures and excessive heat in summer  were some  of the
major factors  which led to deterioration of  some essential parameters of  pot line and finally some pots were  stopped
to survive. However after  de-bottlenecking of carbon plant, the inputs like  anode and bath are matching to pot line
requirement.  Similarly, addition of billet  casting facility and Strip  Casting plant are  helping to evacuate the hot metal. 
With the improved grid position, it is expected to operate the plant in future without much problem.   With the 
expansion of Smelter  the   capacity  of power plant is also being enhanced from 720MW to 960MW.
The Committee was  informed that the  de-bottlenecking of Smelter was carried  out at a cost of Rs.49.12 crore.  This 
was mainly  in the Carbon area of Smelter Plant, which was proving  to be  a bottleneck for the   Smelter plant to attain
its designed capacity.  The de-bottlenecking of Smelter has helped in attaining 480 pot operation (100% capacity
utilisation)  in  Smelter.  No further de-bottlenecking is  planned in Smelter.  However,   for the third pot line under
Smelter expansion, the above aspect has been taken care of. During the course of oral evidence on 10
th April, 2001, the
CMD informed that Nalco is running at over 100% capacity.
The Committee noted that inadequate checks and maintenance caused the shunting of pots in the smelter in April and
June 1998 resulting in less then 100% utilization.
The Committee recommends that adequate safeguards be built within the system to avoid such recurrence in future.

13. Research and Development
Nalco has two independent R&D centers at both M&R Complex, Damonjodi as well as in S&P Complex at Angul. Both
the centers have been recognized by Ministry of Science & Technology, Govt. of India. Both the centers are equipped
with facilities to take care of plant related process, problems and product development activities for value addition. It
also continues to carry out small experiments to improve the quality of inputs in production process, to improve
productivity and quality of product. The R&D center has successfully implemented projects like Special grade Alumina
pilot and commercial plant and Zeolite "A" commercial plant. Further value-added products from waste materials like
fly ash and red mud have been developed. Some process technologies have been patented. Nalco has taken up some
collaborative R&D project with CSIR laboratory, IIT etc. in areas of process and product development. Nalco's R&D
scientists have received national and international awards like NRDC Award, WIPO Gold Medal, ICI Award etc.
The Committee appreciated several of the value added products made from fly ash. The Committee also noted that the
captive power plant of Nalco generates a considerable amount of fly ash which can be used to make value added
products. During the course of oral evidence on Demands for Grants  the CMD stated  "As far as research and
development wing is concerned, we have developed a special grade alumina and Zeolite.  The special grade alumina
project will be completed in December, 2001. Then we have also undertaken research project in collaboration with
Russia. This research project will help converting iron in the red mud to pig iron".
The Committee recommends that Nalco should explore means of using its R&D output for finding viable means to
commercially dispose of the fly ash. Besides the Committee also feels that  R&D effort should be channelised to explore
ways to improve the quality of alumina and other secondary aluminium products. Efforts may be made to complete the
special grade project as per schedule. The Committee also hopes that the research project in collaboration with Russia to
convert iron from red mud to pig iron would be completed early and would be successful.

The Committee was informed   that Nalco has taken over IAPL on 16.03.2000 at an estimated project cost of Rs.292
crore. The integration of IAPL operations will benefit Nalco in view of the synergies in several areas. IAPL will remain
as a separate 100% EOU unit even after merger. During the course of the oral evidence on demands for grants (2001-02)
the CMD of Nalco informed that the process of commissioning of the IAPL plant is likely to be completed soon. The

The Committee recommends that Nalco should make full use of takeover of IAPL by making a strong thrust in the area
of secondary aluminium products and the result should reflect in Nalco’s overall financial performance  so as to justify

15.       Breach of  NALCO’s  fly ash pond at Angul.
The Committee visited  Angul captive power plant on 23
rd January, 2001.  The Committee also visited the fly ash pond
of Nalco and the place where the breach took place. The Committee enquired into the reasons for the breach of the fly
ash pond which took place on 31.12.2000 as a result of which heavy ash with water drained from the pond and a fly ash
flood took place. This had a severe impact on the soil fertility of over twenty-three villages. Acute drinking water
problem arose from  this and around one thousand acres of land got adversely affected. The Committee was informed
that an inquiry Committee had been constituted to inquire into the reasons for the mishap.  During the course of oral
evidence on Demands for Grants of Ministry of Mines the CMD of NALCO  informed that the breach has been
repaired. Regarding compensation the CMD stated: "The district administration headed by the Collector, in consultation
with various MLAs and some important people in the Angul area, has worked out the compensation. We have entirely
accepted the compensation package worked out by the Collector. Out of about 1100 people who have been affected, a
list of about 740 people has been released. We have already paid the compensation to those people for the damaged
crops as well as for the ash that has been deposited on their particular land. The Collector was of the view that 100%
compensation should not be made in the first instance. He says that let them remove the ash that is collected on their
lands first. After they remove that, then we can pay the balance 40%. In addition to that, as a gesture, we have provided
them with piped water supply, costing us about Rs.5.7 crores. It has nothing to do with the breach or the compensation.
We have already paid Rs.1 crore to the Collector. So, whatever compensation was recommended by the District
Administration has been paid by us."
The Committee recommends that adequate safeguards be built within the system to prevent  recurrence of such incidents
in future. The Committee also recommends that stringent  action be taken against the officials  responsible for the
breach of fly ash pond. The Committee would also like to know the recommendations and action taken on the enquiry

18.   Peripheral area development
The Committee was informed that Nalco plays a catalytic role for improving the infrastructure and general quality of
life of the people living in the periphery of the Company’s plants and facilities through implementation of a systematic
programme of periphery development with particular emphasis on rehabilitation of displaced families and weaker
sections of the society. The Committee was further informed that in both Angul and Damanjodi units of Nalco,
periphery development activities are planned by the Company’s peripheral development  Committees in consultation
with local govt authorities.  These  Committees formulate the annual plans and estimate taking into account the needs of
the Peripheral Villages alongwith the views of State  Agencies and  elected representatives of the  localities.  Works are
mostly  executed  through the placement of funds with the local Government  authorities.  However, depending upon 
the nature of the work some of the jobs are directly executed by the Company.  The Company officials monitor the jobs
for which  funds are  sanctioned and obtain execution/completion certificate from the  concerned agencies from time to
time.
The Committee however was not satisfied with the progress made under the peripheral area development programme.
The Committee considers the peripheral area as an integral part of  Nalco and its development would generate
tremendous goodwill for NALCO.  The CMD of NALCO  stated "Every year, we spend about one crore on the
peripheral development of the two projects i.e. Angul and Damanjodi." The CMD also informed "We have allocated 0.5
per cent of the profit for peripheral development. Now we have definitely planned to increase this. Our profits have
increased substantially. We also want to increase the outlay for peripheral development. I am happy to inform you that
the Ministry of Mines has recently taken a very important decision that it advised us to include the local MPs in the
Committees we have set up for peripheral development". "In case of Angul and Koraput, we will include the Members
of Parliament from these particular regions so that they will get an idea as to what the peripheral development would
be."  As regards ex-servicemen and women, the Secretary Ministry of Mines stated  "As far as ex-servicemen are
concerned, we have not taken up anything. I totally agree with you. In fact, there are two shortcomings. One is regarding
the ex-servicemen and the other is regarding women strength. It is also quite low. These are two important
shortcomings. We will take up these two things and do something."
The Committee recommends that greater stress should be placed upon proper monitoring of the peripheral area
development programmes. The Committee strongly recommends that higher allocation be made for peripheral area
development. Besides the Committee was distressed to note that despite Angul area having a large number of ex-
servicemen,   adequate representation in terms of employment in Nalco has not been given to them. The Committee
hopes that adequate representative be given to Ex-servicemen.
19.       Some problems
The Committee   has been given to understand that  NALCO is facing some problems and         their  solution  is 
required  for increasing Nalco's  market  share and  sales revenue. The     problems are :-
Since lot of scrap aluminium of inferior quality is  being imported into the country and is being used by the aluminium
down stream industries, Nalco as a quality conscious primary producer is facing problems in competing with such
upgraded and low quality scrap metal.
The Committee recommends that  the Government may kindly consider enhancing the import duty on such scraps to the
same level as that of primary aluminium metal.
Due to non-uniform Sales Tax Policy still prevailing in certain states, the company is
facing problems in competing with metal  sold/traded  from  these  areas. This  not  only causes loss to the Government
exchequer, due to less tax  realization   but   also  creates unhealthy competition between different
marketing/distribution channels. It was requested that at least for primary aluminium metal, for which there are limited
number  of producers, uniform Sales Tax structure is followed.

The plant for production of Zeolite-A, used in detergent manufacture is in advanced stage of commissioning. Zeolite-A
has been scientifically proven and commercially implemented as eco-friendly material for this application. However,
most of the detergent  manufacturers are still using STPP (sodium tri poly-phosphate), which is a pollutant and,
therefore, has been banned in, many western countries. When STPP mixes in the water system, it helps in growth of
algae, which extracts dissolved oxygen from water, thereby, the aquatic life perishes.

protection, use of STPP may be banned by the Government through an appropriate legislation. Besides, incentives may
kindly be given for use of Zeolite by exempting Excise Duty on this product for a period of at least 5 years.

number of locos to achieve turnaround of Nalco Wagons as planned by RITES.

I,  the Chairman  of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry having been authorised by
the Committee, hereby present this Fifty-fourth Report of the Committee on   the Credit Flow to SSI sector.
 
2.         The Committee at its meeting held on 6
th June, 2001 heard the oral evidence of the representatives of the Associations
of Small Scale Industries and Agro & Rural Industries  and visited Mumbai from 12th to 16th June, 2001 in that connection.
 
3.         The Committee at its meeting held on 12
th July, 2001 considered  and approved Action Taken Report  on  43rd  Report 
of the Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry on Credit Flow to SSI sector.
 
4.         The Committee considered and adopted the Report on 10th September, 2001.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED
BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
 
RECOMMENDATION  No.3
 
1.         Joint Mechanism for appraising term loans and working capital
 
The Committee came to know that there is no single agency for lending the term loan and working capital to SSI units’
requirement exceeding Rs. 10 lakh which leaves the SSI entrepreneurs to run from pillar to post.  Under the circumstances, the

54th Report
file:///D/Committee%20on%20Industry/54threport.htm[04-07-2016 12:13:29]
Committee feels that situation may improve a lot if there is a mechanism for joint appraisal of term lending and working
capital loan for higher amount (about Rs. 10 lakh) so that there is no gap in the sanction of two types of loans.  The measures,
if undertaken, not only will save the time but also the money for SSI entrepreneurs, the Committee feels.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
With  the enhancement of loan limit under Composite Loan Scheme from Rs.10 lakhs to Rs. 25 lakhs, most of the tiny
units would be covered and the problem of approaching separate institutions for meeting different requirements would be
resolved.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION  No.8
           
2.
         Prime Minister’s announcement of package for SSI sector.
 
(i)                   Presently, the Government has given the capital subsidy in select sectors (under Credit Linked Capital Subsidy
Scheme). The Committee feels that Ministry  of  SSI  & ARI   should  examine  whether  such  capital  subsidy  is 
required in other sectors of SSI for technology upgradation, if so, the Ministry should take up the issue at
appropriate level.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
There is scope for inclusion of more sectors in the scheme.  While formulating the scheme, it has  to be acknowledged that
the identification of technology is a continuous process.  The Scheme envisages that a Technical  Advisory Committee would
be set up under the Chairmanship of Secretary (SSI&ARI) to identify the state-of–the-art technology and benchmark existing
and new technologies.
 
(ii)                 The Committee further observes that since sickness of SSI units  is a chronic problem, a serious thought and
timely action is required for rehabilitation of currently sick but potentially viable SSI units.  The Committee hopes
that RBI will be successful.  In its current efforts to draw a detailed, transparent and non-discretionary guidelines
and same will be issued for effective implementation before the sick but potentially viable SSI units  go beyond the
point of no-return.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
RBI has recently constituted a Committee under the Chairmanship of  Shri S.S. Kohli, Chairman, IBA to draw revised
detailed, transparent and non-   discretionary guidelines for rehabilitation of current sick and potentially viable     SSI units.
 
(iii)                The Committee feels that  policy/package which has been envisaged/ extending to SSI will not suffer the problem
of  the implementation of gap.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
Action on most of the  measures announced in the policy package has been initiated/completed.
 
(iv)               The Committee recommends that Ministry of SSI & ARI while furnishing ATN on the recommendations
contained in the present Report will give detailed note with regard to action taken and its impact on each and every
scheme under the present package for SSI units.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
The action on various points of the comprehensive policy package has been  taken  indicated against each in the
Annexure.  The reaction/impact of certain measures  like doubling excise duty exemption limit, enhancing the coverage of
loans under Credit Guarantee Scheme, raising the project cost limit under NEF, launching of  Credit Linked Capital Subsidy
Scheme for Technology Upgradation, has been positive and overwhelming as many prominent SSI Associations have lauded
the Government efforts to strengthen the SSI sector and enhance its competitiveness both domestically and globally. 
However, with regard to other measures,  it is too early to assess the impact.
 
In regard to point   No.15 in the Annexure submitted by the Ministry on the Recommendation No.8, the Committee felt

RECOMMENDATION NO.1 
 
5.         Meeting of Working Capital Requirement
 
The Committee recommends that steps should be taken to ensure credit facilitation to SSI units upto 20% of SSI
production/turnover.
 
5.1       Comments/Action Taken
 
RBI has advised the banks for enhancement in limit from Rs.4 crores to Rs.5 crores for computation of aggregate
working capital requirements of SSI units on the basis of minimum  20% of their projected annual turnover vide circular
No.PLNFS No.BC7.3/06.02.31/98-99 dated 1.3.1999.Following the discussions at the meeting of Group of Ministers on SSI,
RBI has   reiterated the  instructions contained in its circular dated the 1
st March,1999 to commercial banks for providing
working capital based on this specified norm  vide circular No. RPCD PLNFS. BC.16/06.02.31/2000-01 dated 15 th
Sept.,2000.
 
5.2              Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
            During the course of interaction with the representatives of the Banks in Mumbai on  the Committee was informed by
the representatives of the banks that the assessment of the limit, it is somewhat cumbersome procedure but in case of SSI it has
been agreed that 20% of the turnover should be given as a limit and it enables them to look after about 5 cycles in a year. Now
this 20% is of projected sales. It has ben  seen often there are differences of views between borrower and the banker about
the    projections  given  that  creates many difficulties. Apart from that, the procedure is very simple and normally the bank
should not deduct or deduce once they arrive at the 20% of the sales figure. Generally 20%  in all SSI it is a very clear
situation in the bank branches that they have to abide by the Naik Committee norms which is 20% of the projected turnover. 
Now the projected turnover, sometimes people in their anxiety to get a slightly better proportion of the bank finance put it
unrealistically.
 
5.3       The Committee feels  that proper evaluation of the past trends should be taken into account together with the capacity
of the unit  to increase the turnover depending on availabilities of orders and infrastructure to extend the work orders   by the
Banks so as to arrive at a realistic figure regarding the turnover. The Committee recommends that the Branch Managers
should work out a realistic target so that the 20% is met under all circumstances. The Committee also feels that the Branch
Managers who meet their targets should be suitably rewarded.
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.2
 
6.         Sustainable rate of interest:
The Committee not only hopes that the commercial banks will lend  credit to SSI units at sustainable rate of interest
but expects strongly that Government will chalk out adequate incentive to induce commercial banks for extending loan at
sustainable rate of interest.
 
6.1       Comments/Action Taken
 
The Banks endeavour is to charge the most competitive interest rates on advances to SSI units.  Recently, RBI has cut
down the rate of interest by 1% in two phases.  It is expected that the bank will pass it to their  borrowers.  The recent lowering
down  of bank rate will help to reduce the cost of credit  further.
 
6.2       Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
During the course of interaction with representatives of financial institutions and banks the representative from
Maharashtra State Finance Corporation  stated that the health of SFCs is linked to the health of SSIs, When the SSIs do not do
well, the SFCs don't do well. One of the things that the SFC founds itself as the MSFC because of the narrowing gap between
the borrowing cost and the lending rate of interest that is inter spread. The overall cost of borrowing ranges between 8-10%
while the overall cost of borrowing is 13.50%. The main source of raising funds is the re-finance from SIDBI and IDBI which
charge something like 11.5% and 12.5% respectively. The State Government charges a guarantee fee of 2% so that raising the
cost of borrowing is 13.5%. The interest spread therefore that is available even if they  take only 1.5%, they  can only lend at
15%. In a regime of falling interest rates in the market if  they lend at 15%, and that is the least rate they can lend at, what

54th Report

really happens is that good borrowers repay faster and the other problem is that SIDBI and IDBI do not retire high cost funds.
 
6.3       The Committee has noted with concern the narrowing gap between the cost of borrowing and the cost of lending for
financial institutions. The Committee recommends  the possibility  should be explored by SIDBI and IDBI to retire the old
high cost dues so as to facilitate the fresh loan process and give impetus to SSIs. The Committee also recommends that steps
to  evolve necessary mechanism so that the financial health of SFCs is restored.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO. 4
 
7.           Wider  Access to Bank Finance
 
The Committee strongly feels that the Govt. should undertake following measures for enabling SSI units to have access to
bank finance-
 
 (i)        Undertaking of orientation course and adequate training for staff/officers of commercial banks for a change in the
attitude for lending to SSI sector.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
(i)             As per the periodical reports received from RBI, regular  training programmes are  organised  by  the Banks for 
staff/officers so as to improve their work performance besides sensitising them towards better service delivery to
SSI sector.
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee has observed that a change in the mental attitude of the bank officials at the lower levels is required. The
Bank officials should take a proactive role in encouraging entrepreneurship and provide both technological advise and
financial inputs to make the SSI sector strong.
 
 
(ii)                 Simplification of procedures for obtaining credit from Banks.  Arrangement may be made for land mortgage
instead of stamp duty for enabling SSI units to obtain credit from bank against land mortgage.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
As per the periodical  reports received from RBI banks, there is   continuous endeavour to simplify their procedures
with a view to prompt and efficient service to the SSI units.
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee has noted that an entrepreneur has still to run from pillar to post and completing all procedural
formalities is still a nightmare. The Committee recommends that further simplification of the procedure may be done on an
urgent and priority basis.
 
(iii)                Govt. should create conducive climate for development of factoring services through appropriate policy
prescription/ legislative changes to ease problems relating to stamp duty, registration fee, assignment of Debt
etc.
 
Comments/Action Taken
 
The Ministry of SSI & ARI has constituted a Committee on factoring services  under the Chairmanship of Joint
Secretary.  The Committee has prepared a draft legislation on factoring services which is under consideration of the GOI
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee would like to know the latest status of the above draft legislation including the steps taken by the
Ministry to expedite the consideration and approval of the legislation.

(iv)               Recapitalisation  and revamping of SFCs with the help of SIDBI and IDBI enabling SFCs to lend fixed capital
to SSI units.

(v)                 Since RRBs are not widespread with branches even in rural areas so well performing RRBs may be

Comments/Action Taken
 
Under the Credit Guarantee Scheme,  RRBs are eligible for becoming member lending institutions
 
Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee has observed that further encouragement is needed for well performing RRBs. The Committee is
distressed to note that abysmal progress has been made in this area. The Committee recommends that credit on soft loan basis
to SSIs in rural areas be given so as to give a fillip to innovation and entrepreneurship in rural area.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.5
 
8.         
Popularisation of Venture Capital Fund
 
The committee feels that the Commercial banks should come forward in launching venture capital funds in all its
comprehensiveness so as to effectively integrate and enhance the opportunities for SSIs in domestic and international market.
 
8.1       Comments/Action Taken
 
The matter has been taken up with Department of Economic Affairs (Banking Division). The Ministry is also
discussing with SIDBI, other financial institutions and SSI Associations.
 
8.2       Further  Observations/Recommendations
 
The Committee is constrained  to note that the majority inputs by venture capital has taken place in areas other than SSIs.
The Committee would like to be informed of the output of the discussions initiated with SIDBI and other financial institutions.
The Committee recommends that steps to build up a strong culture of venture capital for SSIs is required to be built up.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.6
 
9.
         Setting up of Technology Upgradation and Development Banks
 
9.1       Although SIDBI has come forward with Technology Development and Modernisation Fund (TDMF) Scheme in order
to assist SSIs at its prime lending rates but the Committee,  taking   into   account   the   magnitude   of  the problem of
technological  obsolescence in SSI sector, feels that Govt. should come forward to set up Technology Upgradation and
Development Banks to take stock of ground realities of sickness of SSI units due to obsolescence of technology and assist the
units by ensuring credit facilitation at appropriate time and thus save the sick but potentially viable SSI units before dying out.
 
 
9.2       Comments/Action Taken
 

54th Report

RBI has advised the banks to develop schemes to encourage investment by SSI units in technology upgradation vide
circularNo.RPCD.PLNFS.BC.16/06.02.31/2000-01 dated the 15 th September, 2000.  Besides, Ministry of SSI & ARI  has
launched in October, 2000 a Credit Linked Capital Scheme for new and existing SSI units for technology upgradation.  In
view of these, there is perhaps no case for setting up Technology Upgradation and Development Banks for the present.
 
9.3       Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
The Committee has noted that there has been increase in the NPAs of banks in the recent past. With the increasing
competition arising after WTO and the huge influx of imports from China there is a need to provide technological leadership
to the SSIs. During the course of interaction in Mumbai the representative from the bank stated that Technological leadership
at the district level is the most important thing. Unless the technological leadership is given, the branch manager will not find
the confidence to give money.  The other point is that in the ground level some kind of machinery where investor or self
employed would  get advice to invest. Therefore technological advice is the most important thing.
 
9.4       The Committee recommends that adequate steps to provide technological inputs to SSIs need to be given so as to
enable them to face global competition. The ministry can make a think tank with adequate support so that flow of latest
technology takes place.
 
 
RECOMMENDATION NO.7
 
10.       
Extension of non-financial services
 
The Committee feels that banks need to play the role of a friend, philosopher and guide to their clients.
 
10.1     Comments/Action Taken
 
Banks staff/officers are  being trained and sensitised towards SSI loaning and credit friendly environment.
 
10.2
          Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
The Committee is distressed to note that a lot remains to be done to sensitize the Banks staff/officers at the ground and
cutting edge level. The issue of granting loans without collateral security still poses a big problem.  An entrepreneur has to
really struggle hard  to get a loan sanctioned. The Committee has noted with concern that there are constant complaints that
deposits and collateral are being asked for. During the course of interaction in Mumbai the Committee was informed that some
banks like the Bank of Baroda have done exceedingly well by introducing innovative concepts like PMRY clubs where the
recovery and performance seems to be much better.
 
10.3     The Committee recommends that concrete steps to make the lower level bank staff more responsive  are required to
make a real difference at the  grass root  level are to be given special recognition in the form of annual certificate award etc.
and  the Committee also recommends that cases of banks who have been particularly successful need to be emulated and
followed up by other banks.

RECOMMENDATION NO.11
 
12.       The Committee while expressing serious concern over accumulation of inventory to the tune of Rs.750 crore
recommends that the KVIC should take an all out efforts for clearing all the inventory in the minimum possible time.  The
KVIC should sketch effective marketing strategy for clearing the stocks which has piled up over the years.
 
12.1     Comments/Action Taken
 
The KVIC has started engaging designers so to give a boost for readymade garments and to increase the sale of khadi. 
The KVIC has also participated in various fairs/exhibitions organized by the ITPO, CII, Centre for Bhartiya Marketing
Development (CBMD) in various parts of the country.
 
12.2     Further Observations/ Recommendations
 
The Committee desired to know the details of the response to the fairs. The Committee has noted with serious concern
that KVIC continues to have huge inventories and it reflects on the lack of marketing expertise within KVIC. The Committee
also feels that KVIC has not been able to change according to the market demand and has not been able to develop a suitable a
marketing strategy. The Committee recommends that immediate steps to evolve a effective strategy be taken in this regard.

RECOMMENDATION 
Steps to Increase Demand 
Government may take following steps in order to increase the consumption of steel which 
will automatically increase the demands of steel in various sectors of economy:-
(i) Envisaging Mega- infrastructural projects like roatl. Power ports, dams, water 
pipelines, Airports etc and speedy implementation of these projects say in 3 to 5 
years; 
(ii) Reduction in safe life of LPG cylinders from existing 20 years to 15 years; 
(iii) Promotion of made in India Steel for infrastructure projects, especially those 
projects which are financed 100% by Indian Companies . Made in India steel 
must be used for construction of bridges and roads. 
(iv) .Encouraging the use of steel wheelbarrows instead of allowing to carry material 
on head; 
(v) Replacement of the use of bamboo scaffolding by steel pipe structure; 
(vi) Banning usage of health hazardous asbestos corrugated sheet both for domestic 
and industrial cladding purpose; 
(vii) Promotion of steel usage in making of truck body; and 
(viii) Encouraging usage of steel houses in earthquake prone zone. 
The measures above will result into multifold growth in areas like housing construction 
etc. And ultimately gross domestic product with go up, besides improving the health of India 
Steel Industry.

INTEGRATED NATIONAL STEEL POLICY 
5. 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee reiterates the recommendation made in 30th Report ( of Department 
Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry) to have an "Integrated National Steel 
Policy" comprising of all the segments of the Steel Industry and a policy statement which can 
land the Steel Industry to a place where it can open the account in the new millennium with 
cherished vision and rosy hopes and aspirations. Such National Steel Policy, embedded within 
overall national ,policy and priority, should be formulated while keeping in mind the SWOT 
analysis (strength, weaknesses, opportunitie s and threats) of Indian Steel Industry vis-a-vis world 

Steel Industry.. National Steel Policy should incorporate mutual coherence and cp-existence of 
Public and Private sector and reveal the policy with regard to investment-decision, humM 
resource management, pricing-policy in a liberalized and globalised economy, export import 
policy, structural co-ordination between various organizations dealing steel units etc. 
REPLY 
The Ministry of Steel has decided to formulate a National Steel Policy to have ;a national 
perspective and vision for the steel sector in the context of the second generation reforms, 
restructuring and globalisation. Ministry of Steel has already set up a drafting. Committee to draft 
a vision statement. The Committee is expected to submit its report within three months. The 
National Steel Policy will be finalised in consultation with major steel producers and consumers, 
their associations, suppliers of raw materials, financial institutions, Ministry of Coal, Commerce, 
Railways and Finance. 
FURTHER REPLY 
In pursuance of the directions of the Parliamentary Standing Committee On Industry, 
Ministry of Steel initiated action to formulate a National Steel Policy. A meeting was held under 
the chairmanship of Secretary (Steel) on 11.10.2000 which was attended by SAIL, TISCO, 
representatives of Planning Commission, Steel Furnace Association of India, CORSMA, CIT, All 
India Induction Furnace Association etc. A small drafting committee was set up to prepare the 
draft. The drafting committee is yet to submit the draft. The draft prepared by the drafting 
committee will be examined within the Ministry of Steel in consultation with Ministry of 
Finance, Commerce, Surface Transport, Railways and Coal. Thereafter, Ministry of Steel would 
go for wider consultation with all the major producers as well as Associations of steel producers 
and producers of raw materials for steel industry. In order to prepare the draft, DCI&S convened

chapters to the experts in the fields. In an era of globalisation any national policy has to take into 
account not only the developments within the country but also developments in other countries & 
especially in view of the integration of the Indian steel industry with the global markets.

RECOMMENDATION 
" The Sub-Committee is constrained to express its displeasure over the low productivity 
of labour in Indian Steel Industry which pushes the Industry to a disadvantageous point. In this 
regard, the respective plant management may be directed to resume that adequate training is 
imparted to the workers & various motivational scheme may be adopted to improve the labour 
productivity.

continue with massive inputs on Scientific Human Resources management in order to achieve a 
'rational labour order' where high labour productivity may be obtained by employing efficient

REPLY OF THE GOVERNMENT 
In SAIL, labour productivity is calculated as "Production of Crude Steel including 
equivalent of Saleable Pig Iron assuming one tonne of Saleable Pig Iron equal to 0.25 tonnes of 
Crude' Steel divided by total number of Works Personnel in position excluding trainees of the 
plants". 
Labour productivity is usually expressed in terms of tonnes of Crude Steel produced per 
man year. The trend of Labour Productivity over the last few years has been as follows:-

The need for manpower rationalisation has been recognised within the company, and 
manpower has been reduced through natural separations, and operation of Voluntary Retirement 
Schemes in phases. 
A Financial and Business restructuring plan for SAIL has recently been approved by the

The incentive and reward schemes that are in vogue for all levels of executives and non­

parameters. Capacity utilisatjon and fulfillnumt of Annual Performance Plan (APP) target on

FURTHER REPLY 
(i) So far as SAIL is concerned the exercise to have rational labour is expected to be 
achieved in the next five years through Voluntary Retirement and other 
separations. This is as per MoU signed between SAIL and Government of India 
in terms of financial and business restructuring plan. 
(ii) Labour productivity depends on various factors like capacity of the plant, 
operating rate, employee's strength etc. Labour productivity varies widely not 
only between India and other Developed countries but also \\-ithin India between

formulate proper 'marketing policy' on the basis of which Central Marketing Organisation should 
chalk out effective marketing programmes which should be delivered to the marketing wing of 
the plant management and plant management should be given sufficient autonomy to act 
prudently keeping in mind the prevailing market scenario . Plant Management must strive at 
product promotion & product diversification & development in order to seize larger international 
market share. A proper market segmentation and brand endowment is the need of hour, besides 
stressing on consumer satisfaction .

which will not only lead to disposal of inventories but also attainment of larger market share.

capabilities/constraints of each of the plant.

compete in the highly competitive market, SAIL is reorienting its strategies/marketing initiatives 
based on the prevailing market conditions.

organisational restructuring consisting of Flat Product Group and Long Product

May 2000 which was attended by Steel Minister, Disinvestment Minister and Chief Minister of 
Andhra Pradesh to discuss the revival plan for RINL (VSP). The information I clarifications 
asked for by the Chief Minister of Andhra Pradesh were furnished to the State Government 'by 
Ministry of Steel and the Department of Disinvestment. It was decided to hold a subsequent 
meeti~g to discus s/ finalise the revival plan for RINL (VSP). The subsequent meeting, which was 
scheduled to be held on 22/23rd January , 2001 could not be held due to the inability of Chief
