convenient to all the concerned Ministers has yet been fixed. 
MANGANESE ORE INDIA LTD. (MOD..) 
18 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee is happy to note that MOIL is a profit making company and 
recommends that MOIL management would make concerted efforts for maintaining its track 
record of making profit. 
The Sub-Committee further recommends that Ministry of Steel should take adequate 
steps to remove the general problems of MOIL enabling the company for better physical and 
financial performance. 
REPLY 
MOIL management and Ministry of Steel have taken following steps for improving upon 
the physical and financial performance of MOIL: 
I. Various technology upgradation schemes are being introduced in a phased manner. 
2. In view of general slow down in the Steel Industry, sale of manganese ore is 
adversely affected. In order to maintain the existing level of productivity the 
company has introduced dynamic marketing strategies such as 
modification/optimisation of product mix suiting the requirements of the buyers, sale 
of individual ores etc. This strategy has enabled MOIL to achieve good performance 
during 1999-2000 and earn a net profit of about Rs. 11.73 crores. 
3. To obtain power at a cheaper rate for its Ferro Manganese Plant at Balaghat, the 
following steps are under consideration: 
(i) To purchase power from outside parties at cheaper rates. 
(ii) To set up captive power plant by outside parties and obtain power on "Build­
Own-Operate" (BOO) basis. 
4. The company has sought exemption from Forest Conservation Act, 1980 in respect of 
its various mining lease of Kandri Mine, for diversion of forest land for mining 
subject to certain conditions. MOIL is pursuing the matter with Ministry of 
Environment and Forests for expediting the decision in other cases. 
5. A team led by Joint Secretary, Ministry of Steel including CMD, MOIL and 
Executive Director (Commercial) had visited China during June, 2000 to promote 
export of Manganese Ore to China and Hong Kong. The response to the team was 
very positive and encouraging. 
6. As a consequence of declaring MOIL as 'MINI RATNA' enterprise, four experts in 
the field of Steel Industry, Management of PSUs, Banking and Finance and State 
Administration have been appointed on the Board of MOIL as part-time non-<>fficial 
Directors to render their services to improve the working of the company. 
7. MOIL has been allowed by the Government to export its manganese ore directly to 
foreign parties. 

FURTHER REPLY 
I. MOIL is purchasing its requirements of power for its 6 mines in Maharashtra and 4 
mines in Madhya Pradesh from respective State Electricity Boards i.e. MSEB and 
MPEB. The average power purchase rate from these two Boards are Rs. 4.50 and 
Rs. 5.30 per unit respectively. MOIL produces 7 lakhs tonnes of cleaned ore per 
annum for which approximate one million units are being consumed annually. The 
cost of electricity for production of one tonne of manganese ore works out to about 
Rs. I 00 which is viable. 
2. For its Ferro Manganese Plant at Balaghat Mine, MOIL requires 2.5 million units 
per month and the Company is purchasing power from MPEB at a concessional rate 
of Rs. 3.60per unit being T.O.D.(Time Off Day) tariff. Ferro Manganese Plant is 
producing l 0,000 tonnes ferro alloys annually for which the cost of electricity is Rs. 
10,000/- (approx.) per tonne i.e. 60% input cost of ferro alloys production. Thus, the 
rate ofRs. 3.60 per unit is not viable for the operation of the Ferro Manganese Plant. 
3. Government of Madhya Pradesh has not permitted setting up of the Captive Power 
Plant by outside parties on Build-Own-Operate (BOO) basis so far. Hence, the 
proposal for setting up of Captive Power Plant on BOO basis by MOIL has been 
kept pending. · 
USHA ISPAT LTD. 
20 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee feels that Usha Ispat Limited is a promising Pig Iron Plant and once 
the cloud of recession is off there would be a new morning for the Pig -Iron Industry. The Sub­
Committee is happy to note that UIL is the first Pig Iron Plant in India to get ISO certification. 
The Government 'should endeavor to encourage all such Pig Iron plant in private sector 
through tax & financial reforms which will not only lead to the prosperity of Steel industry but 
also lessen the dependence on import having its lasting impact on India's balance of payment. . \ 
REPLY 
'Iron and Steel'. including pig iron has been de-reserved and also de-licensed and the 
industry has been thrown open to the private sector for its development. In the post­
liberalisation era, the pig iron industry in India in the private sector has grown many fold. As a 
res.ult of various policy initiatives taken by the Government, the capacity of pig iron in the private 
sector has increased from merely one lakh tpa in l991-92lo over 3.53 million tpa in 1999-2000. 
The contribution of private/secondary sector units in the overall productions of pig iron in the 
country continued to increase. By 1999-2000, their contribution to the total production of 
approx. 3.2 million tonnes was about 60%. Today, India has emerged from a net importer of pig 
iron to a net exporter. 
FURTHER REPLY 
India's export of pig iron during 1997-98, 1998-99 and 1999-2000 were 0.79 million 
tonnes, 0.28 million tonnes and 0.29 million tonnes respectively. The above corresponds to 
about 5% of the global trade during 1997-1998 and around 2-2.5% during 98-99 and 99-2000. 

The Indian Pig Iron Industry, particularly those in the private sector are striving hard to 
reduce their costs of production and be competitive in the market. One of the deterrents is the 
higher cost of imported metallurgical coke which is mainly due to high rate of basic customs 
duty @ 15%. Ministry of Steel has been requesting repeatedly the M/o Finance to reduce the 
customs duty from 15% to 5% which has not been agreed to so far. Further, consumption of pig 
iron is directly dependent on the investment in the infrastructure. construction and engineering 
sectors. It is felt that general improvement of Indian economy and consequent higher domestic 
consumption of pig iron, resulting in higher sales realisation, will improve the performance of 
this sector.

21 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee feels that MPL, being in moribund stage, requires generation of 
new life with enthusiastic management. A policy is required to be taken up. A policy in regard 
to what to do with such moribund plant. The Sub-Committee otherwise strongly feels that MPL 
should be allowed to enliven as there is geographical advantages due to its location. Besides 
workers are willing to work with the management and to undertake all kinds of measures for the 
emancipation of the plant. 
REPLY 
Mandovi Pellets Ltd.(MPL) is a company promoted by Chowgule group of Compames 
and the Government of India. The shares representing Government of India were held through 
SAIL. The shares held by SAIL to the extent of Rs. 2.55 crores were transferred to NMDC and 
subsequently, NMDC made further investment in MPL. The total investment ofNMDC in MPL 
is now stands at Rs. 6 crores. 
MPL has not been doing well and more particularly for the last three years due to 
recession in Steel Industry. The total carried forward loss as of March, 1999 was Rs. 64 crores 
and total liabilities of the company were around Rs. 61 crores. The net worth of the company 
was negative throughout its operating years. MPL have made a critical analysis of the working 
of the company and identified that further investments are required towards captive power plant 
and working capital amounting to Rs. 50 crores. MPL Board debated on the affa1rs of the 
company and discussed the desirability of the pellet plant being synergisttcally attached either to 
a raw material producer or a end user of the pellets who is able to make the required investment 
or arrange for the same. 
As suggested by MPL Board, the possibility of NMDC, as raw material producer, taking 
over the plant has been analysed and discussed in NMDC Board on 9th July,l999 when it was 
decided tha~ NMDC may withdraw from the equity. However, CCL. as the original promoters, 
were prepared to take further risk by making MPL a division of CCL which will enable MPL 
to raise resources based on the overall strength of CCL. The MPL Plant could be revived by 
CCL after it becomes its full fledged division and suitable investment is made for reviving the 
operations. 
In accordance with NMDC Board resolution, Ministry of Steel has conveyed 'in 
principle' approval to withdraw NMDC's entire shareholding from Mandovi Pellets Ltd. to get 
the shares duly evaluated by an autj10rised evaluating company and then come to the Government 
with the final concrete proposal. 

REPLY 
l. Having suffered in the past for many years, on account of non-availabilit)' of required 
electric power, resulting in restricted operations, below 25% of the installed capacity of 
the plant, the MPL has formulated a revival plan which consists of setting up a Captive 
Power Plant of the capacity of l2MW, change in process from Dry Grinding to Wet 
Grinding and refurbishment of the Pelletisation Plant.

TO PURSE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT" REPLIES 
GENERAL RECOMMENDATION 
Provision for sufficient fund-Row at sustainable rate of interest 
2 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee regards continuation of required fund flow as the life blood for steel 
industry which is capital intensive so development and growth of steel industry depends largely, 
on the degree of support from Government banks & other financial institution. Lack of sufficient 
working capitals funds for further modernization projects, high rate interest causing, increasing in 
cost of production due to debt burden & interest multiplication and hesitation on the part of 
Financial Institution in advancing further finance, to several units of steel industry etc. are the 
issues which require immediate reconsideration and evaluation. By the way, the Sub-Committee, 
considering the fact that steel industry, a sunrise industry, is passing through a cyclical recession, 
the financial institution should take a sympathetic view of steel industry & provide: -
(i) find for completion of on-going projects on priority basis; 
(ii) working capital facilities should also be made available at lower rates, because 
the Sub-Committee feels that primary producers find it difficult to extend the 
credit limit to their customers, so banks should be more forthcoming in extending 
working capital; 
(iii) Long term funding should be made available at the rate of 10 to 12% and the 
maternity of such debts may be 8 to 12 years; and 
(iv) As the steel plants has to spend about 15 to 20% of its project cost in developing 
infrastructure such as ports, roads, power distribution, fun"ds used for the 
development of such infrastructure projects may be considered at on interest rate 
of 10%. 
The Su~-Committee believes that the above support to steel industry from financial 
institutions will generate employment & enhance GOP growth. 
REPLY 
Government is aware of the issues which have been taken up in several forums and 
occasions. The issues were raised in the Round Table on Steel organised by the Ministry of Steel. 
As a follow-up of the Round Table, Ministry of Steel has constituted a Project Co-ordination 
Group (PCG) under the Chairmanship of the Steel Minister and Members consisting of 
Secretaries in the Ministries of Finance, Commerce, Power, CEOs of Financial Institutions 
(lOBI, IFCI & ICICI) ,State Bank of India .and President, Institute for Steel Development and 
Growth. The terms of reference of the PCG are as under:-

1. To find ways & means and suggest measures for early completion of the on-going iron and 
steel projects. 
2. To address the problems of existing I newly commissioned iron and steel plants with regard 
to the following : 
a. Demand generation; 
b. Customs and Excise Duty rationalization, 
c. Availability of power at reasonable prices, 
d. Measures to boost export , and 
e. Measures to restrict import of Steel . 
Subsequent to the constitution of the Project Co-ordination Group (PCG), two meetings 
of the Group were held on t 3.3.2000 and 1 I .9.2000 under the chainnanship of Minister of State 
for Steel. Various inputs were received on problems & issues related to the units. Specific issues 
like fund for completion of the on-going projects including their Working Capital requirements, 
lowering of interest rate etc. were also taken up for discussion during the meeting. The 
representatives of the Financial Institutions have generally agreed to provide need based support 
subject to observance of financial discipline by the promoters and also bringing in their equity as 
well as bringing back the diverted funds. The request on lowering of interest rate, however, did 
not find support by the Financial Institutions in view of the fact that this is a larger issue and 
concerns the economy as a whole. 
FURTHER REPLY 
(i) In the two meetings of the Project Co-ordination Group held so far, while no 
categorical assurance has been given to the new/upcoming steel units for 
supplying working capital, State Bank of India had shown its willingness to 
consider financing their share of working capital in respect of some units on 
merits subject to fulfillment of certain conditions. 
The Project Co-ordination Group was mainly constituted to find ways and means 
and suggest measures for early completion of the on-going projetts. As a 
facilitator,' the PCG has succeeded in creating an interface between the steel units 
and the financial institutions/commercial banks to address the problems of the 
industry. The PCG had discussed the problems relating to tenn loan as well as 
working capital requirements of different units with the financial institutions and 
SBI. The financial institutions/SBI have taken follow-up action on the decisions 
arrived at in the meetings ofthe PCG in respect of various units. 
(ii) The Union Budget for 2001-02 has reduced the interest rate on small savings by 
15 percentage points. RBI has also reduced the bank rate to 7%. This has 
resulted in reduction of PLR by most of the commercial banks and financial 
institutions by 0.25 to 0.5%. This reduction in PLR is accordingly, expected to 
reduce the interest rate in the procurement of working capital by the steel plants. 
Interest rates to steel plants vary from country to country and also unit to unit 
depending upon the PLR in the country and agreements with the lending bank. 
These in tum are governed by bank rate and many other factors including 
Government Policy, Reserve Bank Policy, rate of inflation etc. While there is no 
specific information on interest rates being availed by various steel producing 

units in the world, it is a fact that in most of the major steel producing countries, 
the interest rates are much lower than in India. 
(iii) Ministry of Steel at present has no proposal for setting up of Technology 
Development Upgradation Bank to meet the requirement of funds for 
modernisation of steel plants. The integrated steel plants viz. SAIL and TISCO 
are eligible to get concessional loan from Steel Development Fund. In so far as 
newly commissioned steel plants and plants in the pipe-line are concerned, it 
would be premature for them to consider any modernisation at this stage. The 
funds for modernisation of other plants, as and when required, can, be met by the 
existing financial institutions and commercial banks.

Commissioner for Iron and Steel, which may collect and maintain statistics of demand,

II 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee view that Steel Industry being technology intensive Industry, the 
Ministry of Steel should make conscious effort towards technology generation and development. 
The Sub-Committee hopes that R&T Mission backed by purposive service of the 
Empowered Committee, involving intellectual honesty will not only lead to reduction in the cost 
of production but also requisition of indigenous technology, skinned of continuous & rigorous in 
home experiment and research. 
If the fund for R&T Mission, appropriated from Steel Development Fund, is not 
sufficient a result-oriented effort may be made by the Ministry of Steel for getting the budgetary 
support. As a member from Planning Commission is the member of Empowered Committee, the 
Sub-Committee hopes that there should not be too over hitch & hassle for budgetary support. 
The Sub-Committee further views that the Ministry of Steel should make efforts so that 
the benefits of the R&T Mission is available to each and every plant/unit engaged in Steel 
Industry. · 

REPLY 
R&T Mission is primarily to function as the Secretariat of the Empowered Committee 
and wilt do the evaluation of schemes submitted as well as monitoring and assessing of the 
schemes approved. 
2. Normally, the R&D activities in steel sector in the country is carried out by the individual 
steel plants, academic institutes and Research laboratories. In order to supplement research and 
technology development in iron and steel sector in India Government have decided on 19.7.1997 
to spend upto Rs. 150 crore annually from interest proceeds of Steel Development Fund (SDF). 
This money is being utililsed to finance supplementary R&D activities in iron and steel sector, 
both in public and in private sectors, research laboratories and technological universities and 
institutes. 
3. The R&T Mission is giving priority for use of fund for such research projects, which 
address industrial problems, development of indigenous technology, utilization of the indigenous 
raw materials, development of new and value added products, reduce cost of production, energy 
conservation and pollution control etc. 
4. The Empowered Committee has met four times till date and approved 21 research 
projects (II in the Government, 5 public sector, 3 joint (public sector private sector) and 2 in the 
private sector). The total cost o(these 21 projects is Rs.l66.52 crore. Out ofthis, Rs.85.52 crore 
is to be met from Steel Development Fund (SDF). As on 21.9.2000, Rs.50.5815 crore (Rs.0.04 
crore in 97-98, Rs. 1.3798 crore in 98-99. Rs.24.5167 crore in 99-00 and Rs. 24.645 crore in 
2000-01) has been disbursed. No major difficulty is being experienced to obtain fund from Steel 
Development Fund (SDF) for such R&D projects and so obtaining fund from budgetary support 
is not required at the moment. If and when such fund is required, this option will be considered.

(i) The technologies initially selected for the public sector steel plants had become obsolete 
and so gradually, modernisation programme for these plants had been taken up and most 
of them have been completed. The private sector steel plant had also modernised their

The main thrust of the research and technology development undertaken by the steel 
plants themselves relate to innovation in these basic technologies to improve their techno­
economic parameters of operations including reduction in energy consumption, cost of 
production, utilisation of waste materials and control of pollution and also deyelopment 
of new value added products. These are being adopted gradually and the main thrust of 
activities is being carried out by the plants themselves out of their own funds. The

mentioned here that many of these projects are being undertaken by some research and

Ferro Scrap Nigam Limited {FSNL) 
2(i) 
RECOMMENDATION 
(i) Modernisation of Scrap Recovery Technology 
The Sub-Committee was made to understand that FSNL adopted Heckett's world class 
and world wide technology for carrying out the scrap recovery and processing operation. As the 
technology and equipments in FSNL became obsolete and old so it is pertinent that the plant 
should undergo modernisation process at the earliest in order to improve the physical and 
financial performance, henceforth FSNL management should work in the right earnest. 
REPLY 
There is no technology for scrap recovery other than magnetic separation. At FSNL 
magnetic separation is being carried out in mobile separation plants since inception. A feeding 
equipment i.e., Excavator is used for feeding this type of plant. However, FSNL is now setting up 
Modern Stationary Scrap Separation Plants at Durgapur & Vizag. These plants will have 
automatic vibrating grizzly feeder and will dispense with the feeding equipment. Crushing of 
slag and screening to various fractions will also be done after modernisation. 
FURTHER REPLY 
(i) Present status of Modern Stationary Scrap Separation Plant at DURGAPUR is given as 
under:-
All civil and structural drawings and detailed engineering have been completed. Tenders 
for civil construction and structural fabrication and erection jobs have been issued and work 
orders are expected to be released by end of March 200 I. 
All the equipment such as vibrating grizzly feeder, vibrating pan feeder, vibrating screen, 
belt conveyor components, rotary drum magnet, motors, control panels etc. are indigenously 
available and these have already been ordered and are expected to be received by August 200 I. 
Project cost of Plant is expected to be Rs.4.00 crores. 
VIZAG: 
Stationary plant is not proposed to be set up at present at Vizag Steel Plant because it has 
not been found to be economically viable due to very low scrap content in the L.D. Slag. 

Existing 3 Nos. mobile magnetic separators are adequate for fulfilliDJ the requirement of 
Visakhapetnam Steel Plant. 
TECHNOLOGY 
The technology involves automatic feeding of slag mixed with scrap by grizzly feeder 
into the feed hopper, separating metallics from slag by rotary magnetic drum separator and 
screening of the separated scrap into different sized fractions for reuse in Steel Melting Ship, 
Blast Furnace and Sintering Plant or for marketing. This is a proven technology established 
world over by M/s. Heckett Multiserv, who are the world leader in the area of scrap recovery and 
processing in steel plants. Same technology as used by M/s. Hec:kett Multiserv has been adopted 
and therefore there is no doubt about the usefulness of this proven technology in carrying out 
scrap recovery and processing to the full satisfaction of the Steel Plants.

MAHARASHTRA ELECTROSMELT LTD. (MEL) 
19 
RECOMMENDATION ·. 
The Sub-Committee views that Ministry of Steel would take adequate steps towards 
installation of 30 MW captive power plant at MEL plant. 
MEL is a power-consuming unit where approx. 50-55% cost of production is the cost of 
power. State Electricity Board is increasing the power tariff on quick interval which in turn 
affects the profitability of MEL. Henceforth own captive power generation by immediate 
installation of 30 MW power plant at MEL is the need of hour for the survival of MEL. 
REPLY 
Maharashtra Elektrosmelt Ltd. (MEL) a subsidiary of SAIL has been incurring losses 
continuously since 1998-99. The accumulated losses of .MEL were Rs.6.88 crore in FX 99. The 
FY.2000 losses were about Rs.l6.10 crore. Meanwhile, SAIL had converted its existing loan of 
Rs.l4 .crore granted to MEL .into equity capital of MEL in FY 2000 in order to avoid MEL being 
referred to BIFR. 
The key success factors for the ferro-alloy industry are availability of good quality raw 
material and cheap power. The power cost for MEL, on account ofMSEB, at present is Rs.3.44 
per unit. Majority of the ferro-alloys manufacturers without their own captive power capacities 
have located themselves in West Bengal and have a major cost advantage affecting MEL's 
profitability. 
Therefore, availability of cheap power is critical for long term viability of MEL. The 
total power requirement of MEL is about 30 MW. A Greenfield 3.0 MW power plant would 
require an investment .of about 120 cr. MEL will with its current financials will not be able to 
make such huge investments. Given current and projected financial position. SAIL is in no

Rationalisation of Freight 
10 
RECOMMENDATION 
During the course of interaction with workers and management the Sub-Committee came 
to know that freight charges are increased almost every year and as a result the steel industry has 
to face the consequences of high transportation cost. It is a matter to understand that steel industry 
being a heavy industry cost of transportation is itself high and if the freight is increased year after 
year it would be disastrous for steel industry. 
Moreover Sub-Committee has been apprised that in many a cases Railways charges the 
freight for the distance covered plus 30% which is illogical and unscientific. A case in this regard 
may be referred to the K.K. line ofVizag steel plant where RINL has to pay high charges to the 
Railway despite the fact that the cost of laying the rail platform has been realized much earlier. 
The Sub-Committee recommends that the Ministry of Steel should take up the issue of 
rationalization of freight charges in general and the case of K.K. route in particular, ~ith the 
Ministry of Railway at the earliest and resolve the issue without much delay. 
REPLY 
The Railway have been charging freight on Kimadul-Kottavalasa line (SE Railway) by 
inflating the distance by 30% NMDC has been representing for tbe removal of the same in view 
of the increased traffic handled on the line. 
The inflation in distance on K-K line had been continuing since 1967. Initially it was 
65.2%, but with the traffic volume increasing, this was reduced to ·30% in 1981.This percentage 
of inflation has been continuing since then. In the last eighteen years there has been significant 
increase in the traffic handled on K-K Line - originating iron ore movement has gone up from 
56.361akh tonnes in 1987-88 to 117lakh tonnes in 1997-98 and 124lakh tonnes in 1999-2000. In 
addition, the line has been handling other traffic particularly on account of the NALCO's alumina 
plant near Koraput. 
In addition to the budgetary increase in the freight charges over the years since 1981, 
Railways had been revising the classification of iron ore upwards resulting in further increasing in 
the freight charges. The classification of iron ore which was 110 in 1989-90 had increased to 120 
in 1994-95 and 125 in 1999-2000. For the FY 2000-2001, the Railway freight has been increased . 
by about 5% with downward revision in the classification from 125 to 120. The net result will be 
an increase of about 1% in the railway freight for the year 2000-2001 over the 1~99-2000 rate. 
The above two factors have greatly added to the freight burden on the pricing of iron ore 
from Bailadila Sector. 

The Ministry of Steel has taken up with Railways to withdraw the inflated mileage of 
30% on K-K line and freight charged on the basis of actual distance. However, Ministry of 
Railways informed that the concessional rates were granted by the S.E. Railway in 1999-2000 to 
increase the loading from KK line and the results of granting the concessiQn will be reviewed by 
Ministry of Railways at the end of 1999-2000 to appreciate the possible effect of reduction in 
distance inflation. 
Since NMDC have now poised to achieve the loading of iron ore from Bailadila Sector to 
be level of 13.2 M.T. during the current year, Ministry of Railways have again been requested to 
withdraw the 30% inflation in distance on KK line. 
Even, the Ministry of Steel had recommended to the Ministry of Railways to consider 
NMDC's proposal to take over the operations of K.K. line. But Ministry of Railways have not 
agreed to this proposal since the function of rail transportation has been assigned to Railways 
only and moreover NMDC has no expertise to operate any Railway system. The issue will be 
pursued with Ministry of Railways further. 
FURTHER REPLY 
The matter was again taken up with Ministry of Railway. In response, Ministry of 
Railways had intimated about their resource. crunch and advised this Ministry to make use of 
transport capacity available with railways for transportation of their raw material etc. 
FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS 
The Committee feels that Steel being a heavy item even a slight increase in freight will 
definitely lead tQ higher transportation cost and in the ultimate analysis will affect the Steel 
Industry as a whole. That is why the Committee had recommended for rationalisation of 
freight charges. However, it is being felt that further that the Ministry of Steel will continue to 
persuade to the Ministry of Railway for rationalisation of freight charges or to provide 
concessional charges for transportation.of steel products. · 
The Committee notes· the service sector is becoming more and more competitive and 
many steel players have started steel transportation through roadways and if the trend gather 
the momentum there is a possibility that Railways may incur loss. Henceforth, it is in the 
mutual interest of the Railway and Steel lftdustry due consideration is paid by the Ministry of 
Railways towards rationalisation of freight charges, that so, also to attract potential consumer 
to continue Railway mode of transportation and not to let them switch over to Road ways. It is 
also in the. better interest of railway that large volume of heavy/bulky product is continued to be 
transported through railway instead of roadways. 
As far as the inflation in distance on kinnadua1-kotavasala'( K.K. Line) is concerned 
the Committee reiterates that the Ministry of Railways should reconsider the basic issue. Since 
the cost of laying the rail platfonn has been realised much earlier there remains hardly any 
rational ground to support the view of railways to continue for charging freight on K.K. Line 
by inflating the distance by 30% . A rational approach demands withdrawal of such inflated 
freight charges

SAIL holding minority shareholding. The joint venture participation in liSCO is being attempted 
with the idea of facilitating the infusion of fresh capital (by strategic alliance partner), for 
revival/modernisation of liSCO. 

As liSCO is a BIFR case, BIFR was infonned about the Financial and Business 
Restructuring of SAIL/liSCO. BIFR held its hearing on 5th May, 2000 and directed SAIL/MOS 
to submit a final proposal to the Operating Agency (lOBI), for revival of liSCO by March, 200 I. 
SAIL has issued an advertisement inviting "Expression of Interest" (EOI) in Joint 
Venture participation. The last date for receiving the EOI was upto August 31, 2000.

RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee feels that it is an imperative need to arrest the rising cost of inputs 
and negative movement of prices of ASP's product in order to reverse the trend of increasing 
gross loss and net realisation. The said objectives may be achieved by undertaking technological 
innovations and modernisation of manpower through Voluntary Retirement Sch-eme; reduction of 
inventory through strategic marketing and product diversification. 
REPLY OF 11IE GOVERNMENT 
Alloy Steels plnnt js fundamentally uncompetitive because of its location, low quality of 
assets and out.d 1ted technology. Therefore, considering ASP's financial perfonnance in the .past 
and with no str--,:"16 possibility of improvement, divestment of ASP has been considered and 
approved, as pan o1 SAIL's Financial and Business restructuring. 
To reduce losses and to revive ASP in the interim period, an interim turnaround plan, 
prepared by a committee headed by Director (RDCIS), is being implemented from April -
December'2000 by ASP. 
A new Management team beaded by ED (ASP). GM (Works) and OM (Marketing) of 
ASP are overseeing the achievement of objoctivesltargets set as part of the Interim Turnaround 
Plan. The progress is reviewed in the Chief Executives meeting held periodically. 
FURTHER REPLY 
Gives~ the accumulated losses of ASP aad its performance in tbe first half of the current 
fmanciaJ year, it is Wllikety that its divestment will attract any interest from the bidders. With a 
view to rehabilitate ASP, M/s. Dastur & Co. was appointed as technical consultan~ to suggest 
measures to turnaround ASP. The reports ofM/s. M.N. Dastur & Co. is expected to be submitted 
shortly. In the meantime, a taskforce has been constituted to study the approach for scaling down 
production at ASP with corresponding reduction in Manpower and closing down of non·viable 
shops. (Study completed and Report under fmalisation) 

FURTHER RECOMMENDATIONS 
The Committee is of the opinion that Alloy Steel Plant requires consid8J'ed and well 
thought planned revival package . An oscillating approach i.e. sometimes thinking 
resurrection of ASP through disinvestment but at the same time believing that due to 
accumulated losses of ASP (stands at Rs.892 crores) it is unlikely that its disinvestment may not

turnaround plan will arrest the downward financial performance of the Company. However, 
the production level at ASP may be determined at break even points. and ASP management 
may close down non-viable shops. 
SALEM STEEL PLANT (SSP) 
15 
RECOMMENDATION 
The Sub-Committee discussed with workers, officers & management of SSP in detail the 
economic viability and rationale for demand for investment of further Rs. 600 crore for Steel 
melting Shop (SMS) vis-a-vis sluggish demand trend and loan and interest burden to be caused to 
SSP due to proposed installation of SMS and came to the conclusion that installation of -5MS is 
the need of hour. It is noteworthy that out of 48 stainless steel plant all over the world, SSP is the 
only unit without SMS facility. 
The Sub-Committee regards the SSP management's argument convincing which 
underlines the fact that installation of SMS banks on the principles of cost-benefit ratio because 
the existing cost on raw material is 66% of total cost and if SMS facilities are provided, the cost 
on raw material will come down to 45% or so, thus, providing leverage for cOmpetitiveness vis-a­
vis international market. Moreover, the installation of SMS facilities would provide favourable 
Break-Even-Point due to increment in volume of production and reduction in cost. 
Therefore, the Sub-Committee is of the considered view that the Ministry of Steel in 
general and SAD.. in particular should make conscious effort in this regard. 
~ REPLY 
As a step towards backward integration of Salem Steel Plant, steel-melting facilities were 
envisaged to be taken up during the -later part of 9tb Five-Year Plan. Due to fmancial constraints, 
it could not be considered so far. In view of scarcity of resources and high existing level of debts, 
SAIL is unable to provide desired level of funds to various units including that of Salem Steel 
Plant for installation of steel melting facilities, which are essential for technological upgradation 
and long-term viability. Salem Steel Plant is to be hived off inter alia as a part of finaQcial and 
business restructuring proposal. Possibility of forming a Joint Venture Company is being 
explored with two options viz. (i)-steel melting facilities may be set up by the Strategic Alliance 
Partner as a separate Joint Venture Company to supply input materials to SSP or (ii)- a Joint 
Venture Company for entire Salem Steel Plant and the Strategic Alliance Partner will set up steel 
melting facilities in a mutually agreed time schedule.

Ltd (JSL)-ALZ .. The process of divestment has been delayed and is likely to be completed by

General Recommendation 
RATIONALISATION OF FREIGHT 
10 
The Committee feels that Steel being a heavy item even a slight increase in freight wilt 
definitely lead to higher transportation cost and in the ultimate analysis will affect the Steel 
Industry as a whole. That is why the Committee had rQCommended for rationalisation of 
freight charges. However, it is being felt that further that ihe Ministry of Steel will continue to 
persuade to the Ministry of Railway for rationalisation of freight charges or to provide 
concessional charges for transportation of steel products. 
The Committee notes the service sector is becoming more and more competitive and 
many steel player~ have started steel transpo11ation through roadways and if the trend gather 
the momentum there is a possibility that Railways may incur loss. Henceforth, it is in ~e 
mutual interest of the Railway and Steel Industry due consideration is paid by the Ministry of 
Railways towards rationalisation of freight charges, that so, also to attract potential consumer 
to continue Railway mode of transportation and not to let them switch over to Road ways . It is 
also in the better interest of railway that large volume of heavy/bulky product is continued to be 
transported through railway instead of roadways. 
As far as the inflation in distance on kirinadual-kotavasala ( K.K. Line) is COf\Cemed 
the Committee reiterates that the Ministry of Railways should reconsider the basic. Since the 
cost of laying the rail platform has been realised much earlier there remains hardly any rational 
ground to support the view of railways to continue for charging freight on K.K. Line by 
inflating the distance by 30% . A rational approach demands withdrawal of such inflated 
freight charges." 
MANAGEMENT BY OBJECI'IVES 
12 
The Cominittee·hopes that patchy years of SAIL will be over sooner then later if Steel PSUs 
management is honestly guided by the principle of management by objectives then 
management by activities. Memorandum of understanding is a unique tool to evaluate 
performance of a company. Target set, prioritization of parameters and objectives envisaged 
in MOU should act as the guiding force for actual realisation and implementation of 
programmes and course of action. Any deviation from the set target or objective or 
implementation gap makes the hole in the management network reflecting adverse credit in the 
MOU index. It is here that the vision and managerial skill has its role to play. Awarding of 
Fair credit to SAIL in the year 1997-98 and 1998-99 is testimony to the fact that individual 
· PSU management felt to tide over the turbulent water in steel industry, although recession in 
steel industry is a fact. Had the steel PSUs management , under SAIL applied its best, at least, 
SAIL as a whole would have not done so worse as it did actually. However, the Committee 

hopes that physical and financial perfonnance of SAIL as a whole will improve with the timely 
implementation business-cum-financial package for SAIL. 
The case of Alloy Steel Plant (ASP) is a pointer to the fact how the plant continues to 
languish in its physical and financial perfonnance due to the management found wanting in 
their role and responsibility. However, the Committee hopes that New Management of ASP 
will show its managerial skill in handling the situation. As Sub-Committee-! for Ministry of 
Steel visited ASP plant recently the matter will be dealt in a separate Report. 
Similarly, the Committee hopes that financial perfonnance of HSCL will improve under 
new management and with implementation of first phase of financial and business restructuring 
Programmes arid sanctioning of second phase of revival plan which is under the 
consideration of Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance.

existing level of inventories . The Committee reiterates the recommendation made earlier by 
the Sub-Committee that the Ministry of Steel will continue to have periodic assessment of 
the inventories at each plant and will implement effectively the time bound strategic programme 
for disposal of inventories without further delay.

HINDUSTAN PAPER CORPORATION LTD – AN OVERVIEW
 
1.1       Hindustan Paper Corporation Ltd. (HPCL) incorporated in May 1970, is engaged in manufacture of paper,
paperboards, craft paper and newsprint. HPC is a Holding Company and has three Subsidiaries and two major integrated
pulp and paper Mills under its control.  These are:
 
Subsidiaries
 
Mandya National paper Mills Ltd.
Nagaland Pulp & Paper Company Ltd.
Hindustan Newsprint Ltd.
 
Units
 
Nagaon Paper Mills (NPM)
Cachar Paper Mills (CPM)
 
            The production of the Company (NPM and CPM) during the year 2000-2001 is likely to be Rs.424.14 crore.
 
Mandya National paper Mills Ltd.
 
1.2       Mandya National Paper Mills Ltd. (MNPM) was incorporated in the private sector in 1957.  After it became
sick, HPC took over the management of this mill in January 1974 as a result of the tripartite agreement between
Government of Karnataka, HPC and MNPM.  HPC holds 97.8% of equity share capital and entire preference shares. 
The company became sick and was referred to BIFR.  Karnataka High Court have since pronounced winding up of the
company on 20.10.2000.
 
Nagaland Pulp & Paper Company Ltd.
 
1.3       Nagaland Pulp and Paper Company Ltd. (NPPC) is a subsidiary of Hindustan Paper Corporation (HPC).  HPC
hold 95% of the equity shares and the Government of Nagaland hold 5%.  The company which came out of the purview
of BIFR due to financial restructuring again became sick as the revival scheme could not be put into operation due to
law and order problem, lack of infrastructure and absence of banking facilities.  Government has communicated its
stand to BIFR that it will accept any decision of BIFR including winding up.  In the meanwhile, on NPPC’s request
BIFR has asked the company to prepare a revival plan and direct OA to submit a report.  There is no production activity
in the plant.

Industrial Scenario in the North Eastern Region and Sub-Committee’s Findings,
Observations and Recommendations
 
3.1       The entire North East region is very sensitive and has been witnessing troubled socio-political disturbances since
long.  As a consequence, the economic development has suffered badly, resulting in poor industrial growth.
 
3.2       The main reason for insurgency in the North East was the alienation of the people, which began immediately
after independence. The government has taken some initiatives and a sizable number of insurgents have laid down
arms.  But immediately after, they have starting looking for employment.  Internal security problems cannot be resolved
if such issues cannot be addressed.
 
3.3       Every government that has come to power at the centre has been concerned about the development in the North
East but progress has been rather tardy, if not stagnant, despite announcement of special economic packages.  In 1995,
North East Development Bank with an authorised capital of Rs.500 crores was created but how far it has helped
expansion and modernisation of industrial enterprises is not known.  The region still lacks good roads, water and
electricity, the basic needs for development.  What can help boost growth is collection of unspent balance of the
amounts earmarked for different Union Ministries and spending of the same in the region with the emphasis on the
feasible projects and sustaining the existing industries, which are facing difficulties.  It has two objectives – one is the
survival of the industry and the second is the generation of employment.  The main objective is, however, the reduction
of insurgency.  The existing units should be helped so that they can meet the social obligation, develop the area,
generate employment.  Everything should not be seen from the revenue point of view.  Unless existing industries
survive, no investment from outside North East is likely to come as is evident from the fact that after 1997 no new
projects have come to the region.  The fiscal concessions along with peace initiative will change the economic climate
of North East and bring it in the mainstream of country and it will not be viewed as a distant territory.
3.4       The Government of India had granted certain incentives to some specified industries located in the North East. 
Their incentives were mainly in the form of excise duty relief and capital investment subsidy.  The incentives are
applicable only for those who started production after 24
th December 1997.  The transport subsidy scheme 1971 was
also included in the above policy.  This step is in fact to encourage the industrial growth in the North East region.  The
underlying idea behind extending these incentives was to provide the much needed impetus to the North Eastern states
so that the region could overcome its backwardness and the difficulties faced by it on account of geographical isolation
and provide them a level playing field.  The ultimate goal was to facilitate setting up of new industries and sustain those,
which exist thus paving the way for all round economic development of the region.  However, due to the incorporation
of the cut-off date of 24
th December 1997, a large section of the industries in the area prior to this date were left
uncovered by those well-intended notifications.
 
3.5       The industrial activity in the North Eastern states can be attributed to four industries- (a)  forest-base   industries
like pulpwood using paper industries and wood-using plywood and veneer industry (b)  tea plantation (c) refineries (d) 
ancillary and allied  activities based on requirement for   the aforesaid three  industries.
 
Findings of  the Sub-Committee relating to  Pulp  Wood  Paper  Industry
 
4.1       HPC's two mills located in the north eastern sector, having all potentialities to operate at the  rated  capacity,
have been carrying huge liability payable to Government of India, which had accrued during initial  periods of 
operations, when the production did not stablise.  Although  the  production could  be stablised from 1994-95, after
implementation of  de-bottlenecking scheme , the production did not stabilise.  Although the production could be
stabilised from 1994-95, after implementation of de-bottlenecking schemes, the production could not be maximised due
to depressed market conditions.  Now, although the paper market has shown some signs of improvement, it is felt that
because of the cyclical nature of Indian paper industry, the boom period may not last for a long time.  Moreover, the
Indian paper markets, including newsprint market, are closely linked with international paper market scenario, which is

very volatile.
 
             HPC solicits the following reliefs:
 
Restoration of transport subsidy and waiving  of excise duty for Cachar Paper Mills.
Allotment of degraded forest land for raising the captive plantation in Assam.
Timely  allotment of wagons and expeditious conversion of meter gauge railway line to broad gauge in Lumding-
Silchar sector to avoid transhipment.
 
Continuing of Transport Subsidy and Waiving  of Excise Duty
to Cachar Paper Mills
 
4.2       Cachar Paper Mill (CPM) located in the southern part of Assam, experiences more locational disadvantages than
Nagaon Paper Mill and the freight charges incurred by the mill, both for transporting inputs and products, are very high
as compared to other mills.  The paper produced by Cachar Paper Mill is mostly sold in the Northern region.  Due to
higher element of freight, the mill fails to procure institutional orders from Northern region in competition with other
paper manufacturers.
 
4.3       The transport subsidy was introduced by the Government of India to lessen the burden of heavy transportation
cost incurred by the industries located in the North-Eastern sector for movement of raw materials and finished products
from certain selected rail heads.  So far as the locational disadvantages for Cachar Paper Mills are concerned, there is no
improvement in the situation from what prevailed at the time of commissioning of the mill.  Moreover, the freight
charges are increasing day by day, causing more financial outgo from the mill.  The rail head at CPM being a meter
gauge, all the incoming materials and outgoing finished products are transhipped at Lumding which results in avoidable
delay and wastage due to transhipment.  The problem becomes worst during rainy season  additionally due to landslides.
 
4.4       Under the new industrial policy for the North Eastern region, finalised by the Government in December 1997,
the units located in the North Eastern sector are eligible for transport subsidy only for the first five years of commercial
production till 31.3.2007.  in addition, all the units in these zones would be free from income tax, excise, for a  period of
10 years from the commencement of production.
 
4.5       The rationale for transport subsidy is to mitigate the high cost of transportation of raw material and finished
product due to location of the units in remote, hilly inaccessible areas of the country, where the infrastructure is poor.
 
4.6       The transportation cost at NPM and CPM for raw materials and finished products from and to the main lands is
extremely high and hence needs to be mitigated through extension of the subsidy.  The grant of transport subsidy should
be viewed in a different light.  While the units through improved performance may become economically viable even
after tax holiday, the transportation cost does not get mitigated unless the requisite infrastructure is developed.
 
4.7       The southern part of Assam, where the CPM is situated, is highly monsoon prone area and the roads are
inundated with flood waters every year and land slides occur causing disruption of roads movement for about 2-3
months in a year.  Thus, CPM deserves some fiscal concessions from the Government to become a viable unit.
 
4.8       In view of the above, HPC appealed to the Government of India to include the existing establishments which are
continuously being affected adversely due to their locational disadvantages, like the CPM, under the new industrial
policy and grant exemption of excise duty payment for a period of 10 years and to revive the transport subsidy scheme
effective from April 1995 as a special case for CPM.
 
Allotment of Degraded Forest Land for the Development Of Captive Plantation
 
4.9       In order to become self-sufficient in meeting with requirement of bamboo for the two mills of HPC and to
reverse the deficiency of forest resources in general, the need for taking up the captive plantation by HPC should be
recognized and clearance be given.  This also has a beneficial effect to social upliftment due to the manpower required
for this activity.  Since early 1990, HPC has been appealing to the Government of Assam, Ministry of Environment and

Forests for allotment of degraded forest land which needs special consideration to allot sufficient land immediately.
 
Timely allotment of wagons for CPM and expeditious conversion
of meter gauge to broad gauge to avoid transhipment
 
4.10     Cachar Paper Mill is having meter gauge facility and facing tremendous difficulties in getting timely wagon
allotment both for getting inputs and sending out the product.  The rail head at the mill being on meter gauge, all the
inputs and products are transhipped at Lumding, which results in delay and wastage due to transhipment.  It has been
experienced by CPM that after placing the indent for a rail rake, it takes sometimes 3-4 weeks for the allotment of the
rake.  Moreover, the meter gauge rakes are sometimes found to be in a very bad condition.   Due to delay/non-
availability of rakes, CPM has to often depend on despatch of finished products to various destinations by road
transport, resulting in additional expenditure.  In order to have smooth supply of inputs to the mill and despatch of
paper, the following may be consider by the railways:
 
At present, the paper industry is under category “D” and therefore, allotment of rakes gets last priority and takes more
time.  It is thus, proposed that the industries located in the North Eastern region should be given traffic preference on
priority basis, considering socio-economic development of this region, which depends heavily on the major industry
like, Cachar Paper Mills.
In the case of Bamboo, which is the main raw material for manufacturing of paper, priority for allotment of rakes may
also be given considering the extra expenditure involved in road transport.
As regards despatch of finished products from CPM, priority for allotment of rakes should be given considering the
huge expenditure involved in the case of transportation by road.  Further, the wagons have to be maintained in good
condition to avoid damage to paper marketed.
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 
4.11     The Government Policy has been that they have given a one time incentive and some limited time incentive for
development of remote areas.  One time incentive has been in the shape of capital subsidy and the limited time incentive
in the shape of transport subsidy or excise duty exemption or sales tax concession.  For areas like the North East, there
is a continuing disadvantage and if there is a one-time incentive or a limited time incentive it has not taken care of the
continuing disadvantage.  There is always a need for transporting the finished goods because they cannot be consumed
locally.  There are some raw materials, which are to be brought in. if the industries are to survive in the North East
region, then these incentives must be on a continuous basis.  It has generally been seen that a large volume of
investments in remote and under-developed areas did not become fruitful  because of continuous disadvantage of that
area and  could not be underwritten and as a consequence they perished. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends  continuance of  transport subsidy and excise duty exemption to the HPC units located in the North East
region till the relative infrastructural  disadvantages are completely over come as are applicable to new industrial units
under new North East Policy of 24.12.1997.
 
4.12     As regards allotment for degraded forest land for raising captive plantation in Assam, the committee notes from
the oral evidence tendered by the Secretaries, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises  and M/o
Environment and Forests,  that they would see working plans for extraction of bamboo in the North East are approved
expeditiously and permission for construction of dirt road would be granted to facilitate extraction of bamboo from
unexplored areas.
 
4.13     The Committee also notes that the agreement with private firms regarding extraction of bamboo on a long term
basis from the forest areas reserved for the HPC would be reviewed to see whether there are any violations of Forest
Conservation Act.
 
4.14     The Committee was informed that due to local compulsion forest areas could not be leased out for captive
plantation.  The Committee recommends that if land is not made available by the State Government for afforestation,
then the HPC should enter into an agreement with state forest departments to mobilise such plantations with necessary
financial support with the condition that the first charge on the crop at the time of harvesting would be of  HPC.

4.15     As regards availability of wagons etc., the sub-committee recalls that the matter was discussed by the Convenor,
on 21.8.2001 with the Railways.  The committee observes that the response of the Railways was prompt.  The
committee notes that there has been substantial improvement in the availability of wagons and the problem of
transhipment at Lumding is also being addressed to.  The committee appreciates the cooperation extended by the

long way.  The Committee recommends that Department of Heavy Industries should take up with the Railways the

difficult terrain.
 
4.16     The committee felt that there is a need to address the issue of gregarious flowering which could lead to excessive
rodent population and further aggravate the situation.  The Committee, therefore,  recommends that Ministry of
Environment and Forests should address the problem of gregarious flowering, remedial afforestation  and construction
of dirt roads for exploration of bamboo in the inaccessible forest areas.
 
4.17     The Committee also recommends that HPCL should be facilitated in exploring the utilisation of inland
waterways in transportation of its products and raw materials from interiors.
Sub-Committee’s findings relating to Wood-using plywood
and veneer industry:
 
5.1       In Assam about 50,000 people are directly employed in the wood industry and also an equal number of people
are engaged indirectly.  In all 2,50,000 people are engaged in wood industry in the North East region.  The Supreme
Court order pronounced on 31.12.1996 banned felling of trees from forests including private plantations in the North
East states.  The Supreme Court was not informed about the protection enjoyed by the tribals of the North East states
under the Constitution of India.
 
5.2       The absence of gainful employment opportunities has aggravated the disenchantment particularly among the
youth who are lured by the terrorists and anti-national outfits.  The state governments have also lost immensely on
account of non-utilisation of exploitable and renewable resources.  The tribals who used to earn their livelihood by
carrying out forest based economic activities, have been rendered unemployed.
 
5.3       The excise duty exemption and transport subsidy envisaged for new industrial unit being set up under the
Government of India Industrial Policy for the North East (announced in December 1997) have not paved the way for
significant industrial development in the region.  The existing industrial units are becoming increasingly uncompetitive
on account of the general economic slow down and adverse inbound and outbound logistics.  Wood-based industry has,
therefore, requested that the excise duty exemption and transport subsidy, as envisaged in the newly emerging units, be
extended to the existing units, which are teetering on the brink of bankruptcy and eventual closure.
 
5.4       Although wood-based industries had to stop operations in view of the Supreme Court order, the management had
to pay the wages to the employees as per Supreme Court directives.  As a result, the financial health of the plywood
companies has become very poor.  They are in need of restructuring for survival.
 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 
5.5       As regards felling of trees in private plantations, the Committee recommends that M/o Environment and Forests
should interact with the state governments and the industry to reduce the bureaucratic hurdle in felling  plantation in the
North Eastern region and ensure the constitutional rights of the tribals of that region.  With regard to the transport
subsidy and excise duty exemption, the Committee recommends that these fiscal facilities should be extended to these
industries as non-extension of these benefits will make them uncompetitive and may lead to closure of these units and
result in loss of employment, direct and indirect, aggravating the insurgency problem.
 
5.6       Moreover, the Committee felt that in view of the disadvantages due to several factors, a proper incentive-based
financing package was needed to ensure the survival of existing units, which is very vital for ensuring economic
development in the region and also for attracting future investments necessary for rapid economic development. The
Committee recommends that the Banking Division, Ministry of Finance, should formulate an incentive-based financial

package both for term lending as well as working capital, at the same time ensuring adequate collateral to at least those
units which had excellent target record.
 
Findings Relating to Refineries
 
6.1       The major industrial activities in the North East region revolve around the growth and development of four
refineries and petrochemicals plants, which are well established in the region and already have plans to invest about
Rs.3300 crores in the next few years.
 
6.2       The operation of these refineries under the present scenario is unsustainable and as such the companies have no
option and would be compelled to close down the operations in the region.
 
6.3       However, closure of these refineries will result in the retrenchment/redeployment of about 8000 employees in
these refineries apart from a huge unemployment in the ancillary units.  This is bound to give rise to a large-scale
resentment and may become a sensitive issue.  Further, in the absence of these refineries, the crude oil being produced
in the region will have to be moved out of the region and to meet the local demand of the region petroleum products will
have to be brought into the region, resulting in duplication and prohibitive increase of expenditure, apart from the risk of
supply security due to frequent natural calamities and other socio-political disturbances.
 
6.4       Hence it is essential to assist these refineries by way of extending fiscal benefits in the form of transport subsidy
excise duty benefits etc. to make the operations of these refineries viable and to ensure perceptible industrial growth in
the region.
 
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS
 
6.5       The sub-committee observed that there were many refineries established in the NE which did not fall in the
ambit of the existing transport subsidy scheme of the government.  It is the opinion of the sub-committee that the
problems faced by the refineries are not different and hence the transport subsidy scheme should be suitably modified to
cover the refineries located in the NE region particularly due to the huge transportation cost for moving out products
from the region.  This apart, the administered price regime for petroleum products shall cease to be in affect from 1st
April 2002.  The premise on which some of the refineries with sub-optimal capacity were set up in the NE was the
existence of administered price regime.  Hence the cessation of administrated price regime will lead to making these
units unviable and hence leading to their closure.  The Committee, therefore, recommends extension of the excise duty
exemption, transport subsidy scheme and other incentive effective in the NE mutatis mutandis to these refineries. 
 
Creation of Department of  Development of North Eastern Region
 
7.1       With the creation of Department of Development of North East Region, the aspiration of the people of the region
has been raised.  The committee appreciates the fact that at long last this region has received the much needed attention
and it has already got on with the job immediately after its formation and addressed some of the vexed problems which
have not been properly handled earlier. Since local industries and local people are to play a great role in the
development of the region, the Committee recommends that Government should institutionalise an information sharing
and experience exchanging deliberations forum under the aegis of the Department of Development of the North East
Region involving representatives of industrial units and the affected local communities to restore the receding
meaningful economic activity in the region by issuing necessary policy guidelines to all concerned for eliminating the
irritants for fostering entrepreneurial and economic activities.
 
7.2       The Committee hopes that the Central Government will grant economic concessions to the industries in the
North East region without any discrimination, which will help the existing units to survive and bring investment in the
area.  Improvement in the industrial climate and peace initiative taken by the Central Government should go hand in
hand.  This will give industries in the region a level playing field to come at par with the rest of the country.
OBSERVATIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS AT A GLANCE

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
DEVELOPMENT OF AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee understands that the cess of 0.05%, which is being charged at present, needs to be increased to 0.25% for making necessary investment in
testing facilities. The committee agrees with the view expressed by the Secretary that the allocation of Rs.10 crores, that has been made, is insufficient as
R&D and testing facilities have to be enhanced. Therefore, Ministry of Finance may consider increasing  at RE stage.
 
COMMENTS
 
It is submitted that the department has taken the issue with Ministry of Finance in accordance with the recommendations of the committee.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee also agrees with the views expressed by the Secretary that the need of the hour is electric vehicles for having pollution free transportation
in the cities, particularly, in the metropolis.  The Government may consider exemption of custom duty surcharge on items imported for use in manufacture
of Electric Vehicles and reduction of excise duty on Electric Vehicles. The  Ministry of Non-Conventional Sources of Energy may also consider providing
subsidies to the extent of 50% to three wheelers and the Department of Heavy Industry may pursue the matter in this regard.
 
COMMENTS
 
It is submitted that the department has taken up the issue with Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue) in accordance with the recommendations of
the Committee.
 
The issue of giving subsidy to electric powered 3 wheeler has also been taken by this Department with the Department of Non-Conventional Sources of
Energy (DNCSE), who have agreed to provide a subsidy of Rs.1 lakh per three wheeler vehicle with a total limit of 200 vehicles as a part of a pilot
demonstration project.

RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee is constrained to note that out of Rs. 10 crores allocated at BE 2000-2001 only Rs. 1.00 crore was allocated at RE stage.  It is true that it
was a new scheme but efforts should have been made by the PSEs to show good response to the scheme.  The Committee, therefore, feels that at least this
year the response would be better and the amount allocated would be utilized fully.
 
COMMENTS

PSEs UNDER THE DEPARTMENT OF HEAVY INDUSTRY
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            Even after the persistent efforts of the Ministry, the performance of the PSEs has been below the projected levels.  The Committee feels that the
PSEs are required to put in more efforts to usher in a prosperous future.
 
COMMENTS
 
PSEs are under tremendous pressure to perform in an increasingly competitive business/environment. PSEs have been  continuously readjusting
themselves to the changing environment and have been initiating various cost-cutting measures and also upgrading their technology to the requirements of
the customers.  Excess manpower is being reduced to bring down costs.  Business/organizational restructuring is also being continuously undertaken to
optimise utilization of assets. 
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee desires that the  PSUs should take more efforts in :-
 
(i)         Cost cutting ;
(ii)        Upgradation of technology ;
(iii)       Manpower reduction,  and
(iv)       Business/organisational  restructuring.
 
The Committee recommends that DHI should monitor the above aspects company-wise and submit a status report to the Committee.
 
The  PSUs under DHI should evolve  a proper workable mechanism to meet the deadlines for the supply of orders placed on them and fix accountability
for non-adherence to the delivery schedules. 
 
Committee’s further recommendations in respect of BWEL, CCIL, RIC, MDMC, BOGL, PLT and HPF are as under:
 
BHARAT WAGON AND ENGINEERING LTD:
 
            The Committee understands that BWEL (BBUNL) has been short-listed for disinvestment.  In case it is not possible to disinvest BWEL in sixth
months, DHI should expedite the proposal on the turnaround of the company.
 
CYCLE CORPORATION,  MAMC &  RIC
 
            As regards Cycle Corporation of India, MAMC and RIC the Committee understands that on the closure of these three  companies, the statutory
dues to the employees are yet to be paid.
 
            The Committee recommends that the proposal for reopening of VRS/VSS as well as payment of all statutory dues to employees opting for VSS
should be reopened without further delay.
 
BHARAT OPHTHALMIC GLASS LTD.
 
            The Committee understands that a revival plan for BOGL is under consideration of the BIFR.  The Committee recommends that DHI should
continue to give non-plan assistance to BOGL till the revival plan is sanctioned.
 
PRAGA TOOLS LTD.
 
            The Committee understands that Government have failed to find a joint venture partner for Praga Tools Ltd.  In the circumstances, the committee
emphasise that a revised revival plan for the company should be drawn out.  Till then the government should continue to support the company.
 
HINDUSTAN PHOTO FILMS LTD.
 
The Sub-committee-III had interacted with Secretary (HI&PE) and CMD, HPF on the question of the strategies for the revival of HPF on 26.10.01.
 
The Committee observes that HPF is a unique company and the only one of its kind in India.  It caters to strategic needs of the country whether it be
defence or mass health care.  Therefore, a country like India with one billion population cannot be solely dependent on import of photo goods by closing
down the state of the art facilities, which have been recently created with mammoth investment.
 
Present policies of the Government encourage trading/conversion (with value addition of less than 10 per cent).  HPF is an integrated manufacturer with
investment of more than Rs.400 crores in plant and machinery and has necessary skills to manufacture quality products, being an ISO 9002 company.  The
photo goods manufacturing technology is a closely guarded preserve among only a few (6 in all) in the whole world.  The domestic photo goods market is
increasing at around 10 percent compounded annual growth rate and the Government should not lose the hard developed manufacturing expertise of the
last three decades.  In order to encourage integrated manufacturing, it is felt that adequate incentives need to be given to HPF which will culminate in
attracting a prospective JV partner.  In order to facilitate this, the Committee felt that the company’s balance sheet must be cleaned along with reduction in
excess manpower.  It is learnt from the Administrative Ministry that a comprehensive revival plan has been formulated for consideration of the Union

Cabinet envisaging the above parameters.  The infusion of funds requested by the company and the administrative ministry is mainly towards:
 
(i)         One time grant;
Employees related dues;
Attractive VRS towards downsizing manpower;
(iv)       Interest free loan:
(v)        towards working capital; and
(vi)       repayment of old debts of the company (secured and unsecured) mainly to the nationalised banks/ FIs and Government-woned ICDs.
 
The Committee feels that though the total infusion of funds is to the tune of around Rs.560 crores, the bulk of the same (around Rs.470 crores) is towards
repayment of the bank loans.  For revival of the company, the realistic fund infusion is only towards working capital.  The sacrifice on the part of the
creditors comprises 68% of the total dues payable to them by the company.  The thrust of the revival is towards granting specific incentives to an
integrated manufacturer viz-a-viz trading/conversion activity and thereby paves way for a possible joint venture. 
 
            In order to encourage the only integrated manufacturer of photo films in the country, Government should impose following tariff and non-tariff
barriers:
 
(i)         Tariff:
 
Increase n customs duty on imports of semi-finished and finished unexposed photo goods to WTO bound rates by converters and traders, who do not have
integrated manufacturing facility of over Rs.400 crores in plant and machinery and technical know-how.
 
Exemption  on customs duty and excise duty (incl. CVD and SAD) for imports of raw materials by HPF, the integrated manufacturer including colour 
semi-finished goods).
 
Exemption of customs duty on capital goods imports by HPF towards technical upgradation.
 
(ii)        Non-tariff:
 
Designating a single sea port in the country for import of all semi-finished and finished UNEXPOSED photo goods falling under chapter 37 of customs
tariff.
Subjecting all the photo goods imports for random sampling and testing to avoid unethical practices.
 
Imports of all photo goods (semi-finished unexposed) in SINGLE UNIT sq. mtrs instead of currently in different units like kgs, boxes, sizes, packets, rolls,
meters, etc. to prevent loss of revenue to the Government of India.
 
Attractive (1992 wage level basis) VRS to be approved for downsizing manpower and to affect 1992 wage revision to existing/retained employees.
 
Export incentive of Rs.50 per mtr. to be given to HPF towards brand promotion and also ti increase the capacity utilization.
 
Reservation upto 50% of the annual procurements of photo goods by all government establishments and defence organisation for HPF.
 
The Committee recommends earliest implementation of the above proposals  with a view to:
 
(i)         revive the only photo goods company in the country;
(ii)        promote socio-economic development of the region – a backward district in Tamil Nadu and
(iii)       Attract a JV partner who can bring contemporary technology including digital.
 
The Committee further observes that in the event of  closure/winding of this company, the only one of its kind in the country and one amongst the six only
in the whole world, then India with a population of one billion will have to perennially depend on imports for ever and that situation is undesirable,
especially so when the manufacturing technology of photo goods is highly secretive and sophisticated and is available in the country.
 
RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT OF AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee feels that the cess which has been used till now for creating facilities for conducting test as per Central Motor Vehicles Rules needs to be
used for other areas of product and process related research with a view to give a fillip to India’s automobile industries. It is also necessary to enable the
automobile industry to survive the imports surge after WTO regime became fully applicable. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should take
stock of what is being done and what further is to be done R&D has to be undertaken for product and process related research also.
 
COMMENTS
 
The crux of the recommendation of para 3.6 is to take stock of entire Research & Development (R&D) work being done through assistance of cess on
Automobile and steps needed to ensure more effective use of cess funds for undertaking product and process related research with a view to enable the
automobile industry to survive in the WTO regime.  In this regard, it is submitted utilisation of cess funds and the implementation of cess funded R&D
projects is an ongoing process. The projects are reviewed regularly by the Development Council (DCAAI)’s  Cess Committee and recommendations are
made keeping in view the requirement of the industry. The above recommendations of the Committee will be kept in view in the deliberations of the Cess
Committee while reviewing the cess funded projects.

COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATIONS
           
The Committee desires that  utilisation of cess funds should ultimately lead to achievement of  desired results keeping in view the requirements of the
automobile industry.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
The committee feels that the policy compatible with WTO regime should have been formulated much before the regime becomes fully operational. At least
now, there should not be any further delay in formulating the Policy.
 
COMMENTS
 
The Quantitative Restrictions have been removed with effect from 1.4.2001. An Auto Policy incorporating these developments is under formulation.
 
COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATION
 
The Committee stresses that the  auto policy may be formulated without further delay.
 
INTEREST SUBSIDY/GUARANTEE FOR SUBSIDY
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee recommends that there should be proper evaluation and monitoring by the ministry on the restructuring plans.
 
COMMENTS
 
Restructuring plans for the PSEs are being sanctioned/approved by BIFR/Government on a case –to-case basis.  Regular reviews are being carried out by
BIFR with regard to revival plans under implementation and performance evaluation undertaken vis-à-vis the targets projected in the package.  In case of
restructuring plans approved by the Government on its own, reviews are undertaken at the Board level as well as in the administrative Ministry for
initiating necessary corrective actions.  As a result of such reviews by BIFR/Govt/company’s Board, fresh restructuring plans are under preparation in case
of Bharat Pumps and Compressors Ltd. (BPCL), Tungbhadra Steel Products Ltd. (TSP) etc.  Further, cases of Burn Standard Co. Ltd. (BSCL) and
Braithwaite & Co. Ltd. (BCL) have been referred to DOD for undertaking JV formation, following  detailed reviews by BIFR. 
 
COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATIONS
 
            The Committee notes that the cases of Burn Standard Co. Ltd. (BSCL) and Braithwaite & Co. Ltd. (BCL) had been referred to DoD for
undertaking joint venture formation.  The Committee understands that no prospective buyer would come forward to take over these sick companies unless
they are restructured by clearing their balance sheets, giving VRS, fiscal incentive, cash infusion by grants, loans, counter-guarantee, etc. and made
potentially viable.  The Committee therefore recommends that these two companies may be restructured before joint venture formation.  The Committee
also feels that JVP may also be afforded some facilities in the form of Price Preference etc. so as to enable them to come above the initial difficulties.  
 
PLAN INVESTMENT IN PUBLIC SECTOR
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
The Committee recommends that the Department of Heavy Industry should make conscious efforts to utilize the plan allocation made for modernization,
renewal / replacement, implementation of sanctioned revival scheme, etc. so that the PSEs could regain their vigour.
 
COMMENTS
 
Plan allocation for capital investments during 2001-2002 for PSUs under DHI is mainly towards renewals/replacements, modernisation and as per revival
schemes sanctioned by BIFR/Government. A separate head is also available for ‘crucial balancing investments’ to provide funds for debottlenecking and
for any emergency requirements of needy PSUs.
 
COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATIONS
