HINDUSTAN PHOTO FILMS LTD.
 
The Sub-committee-III had interacted with Secretary (HI&PE) and CMD, HPF on the question of the strategies for the revival of HPF on 26.10.01.
 
The Committee observed that HPF is a unique company and the only one of its kind in India.  It caters to strategic needs of the country whether it be
defence or mass health care.  Therefore, a country like India with one billion population cannot be solely dependent on import of photo goods by closing
down the state of the art facilities, which have been recently created with mammoth investment.
 
Present policies of the Government encourage trading/conversion (with value addition of less than 10 per cent).  HPF is an integrated manufacturer with
investment of more than Rs.400 crores in plant and machinery and has necessary skills to manufacture quality products, being an ISO 9002 company.  The
photo goods manufacturing technology is a closely guarded preserve among only a few (6 in all) in the whole world.  The domestic photo goods market is
increasing at around 10 percent compounded annual growth rate and the Government should not lose the hard developed manufacturing expertise of the
last three decades.  In order to encourage integrated manufacturing, it is felt that adequate incentives need to be given to HPF which will culminate in
attracting a prospective JV partner.  In order to facilitate this, the Committee felt that the company’s balance sheet must be cleaned along with reduction in
excess manpower.  It is learnt from the Administrative Ministry that a comprehensive revival plan has been formulated for consideration of the Union
Cabinet envisaging the above parameters.  The infusion of funds requested by the company and the administrative ministry is mainly towards:
 
(i)         One time grant;
Employees related dues;
Attractive VRS towards downsizing manpower;
(iv)       Interest free loan:
(v)        towards working capital; and
(vi)       repayment of old debts of the company (secured and unsecured) mainly to the nationalised banks/ FIs and Government-woned ICDs.
 
The Committee feels that though the total infusion of funds is to the tune of around Rs.560 crores, the bulk of the same (around Rs.470 crores) is towards
repayment of the bank loans.  For revival of the company, the realistic fund infusion is only towards working capital.  The sacrifice on the part of the
creditors comprises 68% of the total dues payable to them by the company.  The thrust of the revival is towards granting specific incentives to an
integrated manufacturer viz-a-viz trading/conversion activity and thereby paves way for a possible joint venture. 
 
            In order to encourage the only integrated manufacturer of photo films in the country, Government should impose following tariff and non-tariff
barriers:
 
(i)         Tariff:
 
Increase n customs duty on imports of semi-finished and finished unexposed photo goods to WTO bound rates by converters and traders, who do not have
integrated manufacturing facility of over Rs.400 crores in plant and machinery and technical know-how.
 
Exemption  on customs duty and excise duty (incl. CVD and SAD) for imports of raw materials by HPF, the integrated manufacturer including colour 
semi-finished goods).
 
Exemption of customs duty on capital goods imports by HPF towards technical upgradation.
 
(ii)        Non-tariff:
 
Designating a single sea port in the country for import of all semi-finished and finished UNEXPOSED photo goods falling under chapter 37 of customs
tariff.
Subjecting all the photo goods imports for random sampling and testing to avoid unethical practices.
 
Imports of all photo goods (semi-finished unexposed) in SINGLE UNIT sq. mtrs instead of currently in different units like kgs, boxes, sizes, packets, rolls,
meters, etc. to prevent loss of revenue to the Government of India.
 
Attractive (1992 wage level basis) VRS to be approved for downsizing manpower and to affect 1992 wage revision to existing/retained employees.
Export incentive of Rs.50 per mtr. to be given to HPF towards brand promotion and also ti increase the capacity utilization.
 
Reservation upto 50% of the annual procurements of photo goods by all government establishments and defence organisation for HPF.
 
The Committee recommends earliest implementation of the above proposals  with a view to:
 
(i)         revive the only photo goods company in the country;
(ii)        promote socio-economic development of the region –a backward district in Tamil Nadu and
(iii)       Attract a JV partner who can bring contemporary technology including digital.
 
The Committee further observes that in the even of closure/winding of this company, the only one of its kind in the country and one amongst the six only

SIXTH REPORT OF THE COMMITTEE 
I, the Chairman of the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry 
having been authorised by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf , present this Sixth 
Report of the Committee on the Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructuring) and 
Miscellaneous provisions (Amendment) BilL 1993. "To be introduced in the Lok Sabha". 
2. The Bill which was to be introduced in Lok Sabha, was opposed at the introduction stage 
and was not introduced. It was thereafter, referred to the Committ ee for examination and report 
through separate paras published in Rajya Sabha/Lok Sabha Bulletins Part II dated the lOth 
January and 13th January, 1994 respectively. 
3. The Committee at its first meeting held on 17th January , 1994 hdd a general discussion on 
the said Bill including the procedure to be adopted by the Comm itte e t o dea l with the subject. In 
the afternoon session of the same meeting the Committee heard the oral evide nce of the 
representatives of Central Trade Unions and the Workers' Unions ope rating at liSCO, Burnpur. 
4. The Committee at its second meeting held on 18th January, 1994 heard the oral evidence of 
the representatives of the Ministries of Steel. Law, Justice and Company Affairs and a lso the 
representatives of the II~CO and SAIL management on the need to bring the new le;Islat ion 
under reference. The discussion was not concluded and the Committee decided to hear these 
witnesses again for further clarifications on the subject. The discussion continued on 9th a11J lOth 
February, 1994 and concluded thereafter. 
5. The Committee while considering the said Bill, also heard the ora l evidence of the Fin a 1 ~·~...: 
Secretary and Special Secretary, Planning Commission with regard to budgetary/funds allocation 
in respect of modernisation of liSCO. 
6. The Statement of Objects and Reasons of the Bill provides that due to unsatisfactory 
management and deterioration in the condition of the plant leading to decline in the company's 
performance, Government took ove1~ the management of Indian Iron and Steel Company 
(liSCO) in 1972. Parliament enacted the Indian Iron and Steel Company (Taking Over of 
Management) Act, 1972 in this behalf. The share capital of the company was also acquired by 
Government in 1976 through the Indian Iron and Steel Company (Acquisition of Shares) Act, 
1976. All the shares held . by the Central Government in liSCO were transferred to the Steel 
Authority of India Limited (SAIL) by the Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructur­
ing) and Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1978 and liSCO became a wholly owned subsidiary of 
SAIL. 
The object of take over of liSCO was to secure proper management of the affairs of the said 
company and continuity and development of production of steel through programmed invest­
ments on modernisation of the steel works. Since the take over of the said company a capital 
expenditure of around Rs. 600 crores has been incurred i n this company mainly for plant , 
rehabilitation, maintenance and undertaking prelimi nary and e nabling works as a prelude to 
modernisation of the steel works. 
One of the main purposes of take over of liSCO was its modernisation which could not be 
achieved due to severe financial constraints. The company"s performance , therefore , continued to 
decline over the years and its has incurred accumulated losses of over Rs. 800 crores as on 
31.3.1993. 

To achieve the objective of modernisation of liSCO in a time bound manner, it is proposed to 
allow private sector participation through transfer of shares. While doing so it will be ensured 
that the assets of liSCO and the interests of the workers are fully protected. 
The Bill seeks to amend the Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructuring) and 
Miscellaneous Provisions Act, 1978, to allow transfer of shares of liSCO by SAIL and to impose 
certain restrictions on further transfer of shares and capital assets of liSCO . 
7. The Committee considered the draft Report at its sitting held on the 15th March, 1994 and 
decided to seek further extension of time for presentation of the report by the last day of next 
Session of Parliament. The Committee again reconsidered the matter on 17th March, 1994 and 
decided to constitute a Sub-Committee of the Committee to reformulate the draft report and also 
seek extension of time for presentation of the Report on the Bill by the last day of the next 
Session of Parliament. Accordingly, the Chairman of the Committee constituted a Sub­
Committee of nine Members, 6 from Lok Sabha and 3 from Rajya Sabha with following 
composition:-
!. Shri Manoranjan Bhakta, Member, Lok Sabha. 
2. Shri V. Dhananjaya Kumar, Member, Lok Sabha. 
3. Shri Manjay Lal, Member, Lok Sabha. 
4. Shri Tej Narayan Sing, Member, Lok Sabha. 
5. Shri P.G. Narayanan, Member, Lok Sabha. 
6. Shri Bolla Bulli Ramaiah, Member, Lok Sabha. 
7. Shri Jibon Roy, Member, Rajya Sabha. 
8. Shri K.K. Veerappan, Member, Rajya Sabha. 
9. Shri Rajendra Prasad Mody, Member, Rajya Sabha. 
Shri Bolla Bulli Ramaiah was nominated as convener of the Sub-Committee . 
8. The Sub-Committee discussed the subject alongwith other relevant papers at its meeting held 
on 24th March, 1994 and reformulated the ·report. The Sub-Committee directed that the Report, 
as re-drafted, may be circulated for the consideration of the Committee. The Committee 
considered and adopted the draft report at its meeting held on the 30th March, 1994 and 
authorised the Chairman and other Members to present the same to the Parliament on 
19th April, 1994. 
9. The Committee considered and examined the following documents received from the 
Ministry of Steel in connection with the Bill:-
(i) Indian Iron and Steel Company (Taking over of Management) Act, 1972; 
(ii) Indian Iron and Steel Company (Acquisition of Shares) Act, 1976; 
(iii) The Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructuring) and Miscellaneous Provisions 
Act, 1978; 
(iv) Report of the Committee of Experts on private Participation in the Indian Iron and Steel 
Company Limited, submitted to the Government of India (Two volumes); 
(v) Information Memorandum on the Indian Iron and Steel Company Limited; 
(vi) Minutes of the meeting of the Public Investment Board (PIB) regarding liSCO; 
(vii) Modernisation proposal prepared by SAIUDasturco, which PIB had cleared; 
(viii) Valuation report prepared by MECON; and 
(ix) Evaluation Report prepared by SAIL and MECON on Mukand proposal. 
10. Besides, the Committee considered a memorandum submitted by liSCO Officers' 
Association. 

11. The Committee also referred some questionnaire received from the members of the 
Committee to the ministry of Steel for written replies and examine d the replies received from 
them. 
12. On the basis of the documents received from the Ministry of Steel and the evidence of 
representatives of Steel Ministry and SAil/liSCO management, the Committee has gathered 
that liSCO is one of the oldest steel companies in India with captive iron ore and coal mines, a 
foundry works and a fully owned subsidiary engaged in production of pipes. The principal unit of 
the company is the Burnpur Steel Works, which achieved and susta ined a production level of 
about 1 million tonnes of ingot steel and 0.8 million tonnes of finished steel in 1962-63 and 
1963-64. Thereafter, the company ran into serious mismanagem~nt. Government of India had , 
therefore, to intervene in the matter and accordingly nationalised the company in 1976 for the 
purpose of modernising the Burnpur Steel Works. liSCO has however been incurring losses for 
last about 15 years despite of Governments' efforts to check the same. 
12.1 According to the Government it stands Committed to the modernisation of the 
company but no scheme could be sanctioned for implem entation, basically due to resource 
constraints of Government and Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL) unwilling to undertake 
the work without budgetary support. Therefore, Government proposes to allow private 
participation in the equity and management of liSCO so that the liSCO is modernised and 
prodcution reaches to the desired level within a time frame and also to ensure that the private 
participant is restrained from disposing the shares of liSCO that he may have acquired from 
SAIL as also the assests of liSCO until the responsibility of modernisation is fully met by him. 
12.2 Government have highlighted the following salient features of proposed legislation by 
amending Public Sector Iron and Steel Companies (Restructuring) an J Miscellaneous Provisions 
Act of 1978:--
(a) The aforesaid Act of 1978 provide for transfer d shares held by Central 
Government in liSCO to SAIL by making liSCO a sub~.Jdiary of SAIL. The present 
Bill enables Govenment to allow SAIL to tn1ns1cr ts shares in liSCO to any person 
including private parties (Amendment to Section 11). 
(b) A new Section i.e. 11 A is proposed to be inserted in Act of 1978 which would 
impose certain restrictions on the person to whom shares are transferred with 
respect to (i) further transfer of shares to any other person and (ii) transfer by sale 
etc. of capital assets of liSCO. The new legislation also proposes to exclude 
employees of IISCQ to whom SAIL may transfer shares from the restriction on 
furth er transfer. 
(c) The new Bill proposes to amend Section 22 of the Act of 1978 providing to exempt 
SAIL from taxes, duties etc. which may be leviable on transfer of capital assets from 
IISCO to SAIL or any of SAIL's subsidiaries. 
(d) The Bill proposes to exclude the private party to whom the share are transferred, 
from the benefit of exemption of taxes , duties etc. 
12.3. The Committee has been informed that even after the entrustment of management to 
SAIL, and a capital investment of around Rs. 600 crores made for rehabilitation of the plant 
upkeep of the health of plant and machinery and preliminary and enabling? works for the 
modernisa tion of Burnpur Steel Works, financial performance did not improve and the company 
contined to be sick, marked by technological obsolescenc e, outmoded work practice, declining 
profitability etc. Several studies have been conducted since 1977 for modernising the company but 
the resource constraints always came in its way. As on 31.3.1993, the cQmpany has an 
accumulated loss of over Rs. 816.00 crores and a negative net worth of over Rs. 433 crores. 

12.4 As per the Government 's proposal for modernisation of liSCO before the Public 
Investment Board the modernisation cost of Rs. 6520 crores is expected to be financed in the 
following manner:-

The PIB , while exammmg modernisation proposal of liSCO was also informed about 
modernisation proposal of Mls Coparo Group Limited. 
12.5 The Secretary of Ministry of Steel during his deposition before the Committee informed 
that the total losses that have been incurred by SAil so far were over Rs. 1000 crores, including 
the writeoff of Rs. 250 crores. While liSCO was continuing to incur losses, SAIL made efforts to 
prepare modernisation programmes. Several studies were conducted and every time a study was 
made , a proposal was also made and the Ministry aproached the Government for budgetary 
support but funds were not made available. Even in 1991 when PIB was approached for clearance 
of modernisation proposal, the SAIL was not in a position to raise .any of the resources, either 
from the budget or loan from the market. In such situation the only possibility was to bring in 
private participation so that modernisation of the liSCO could be arranged. 
12.6 The representatives of the Workers' unions during the course of their oral evidence 
before the Committee, altogether opposed Govenment's move to privatise liSCO According to 
them during all these years they have been requesting Government, not to throw liSCO in 
private hands and instead find ways and means to modernise the company . The main reason for 
liSCO incurring losses is the loans extended to it in past by Government. Government has 
committed blunders by trying to compensate losses through loans instead of going for 
modernisation of the company. The solution could have been to write-off the loans and make the 
company viable by modernising it. SAIL, having a team of experts, has the capability to 
undertake the modernisation plan and the company could be made viable by other proposals 
which can be utilised by the country to keep the undertaking in the public sector . The Workers' 
Unions have all kinds of doubt about capability of any other party than SAIL to undertake 
modernisation of the plant. According to them the report of Committee of Experts is totally 
invalid as excep t one, nobody in the Committee had any experience in the steel industry and the 
only technical member of the Committee has given his note of dissent not having agreed with the 
recommendations of the Expert Committee . The Workers' Unions expressed before the 
Committee that when SAIL is capable of undertaking modernisation of other integrated ste~l 
plants like Durgapur, Rourkela and Bokaro Plants why not the liSCO be handled by it? 
On being asked whether Worker's Cooperatives could take up the plant, the representatives 
deposed that they are prepared to have a joint management of Workers and Executives. 
However, the concept of workers cooperatives is not workable in view of heavy funds required 
for running the company. They also expressed their strong will to jointly work out proposals for 
modernisation of the company. However, according to them the step to privatise the steel 
industry would be very ludicrous and harmuful to the country. 
At a later stage the workers' unions sent a written representation to the Committee 
conveying their willingness to have equity participation of 50 per cent with SAIL in liSCO and 
their full co-operation in the modernisation of the plant. 
12.1 The Finance Secretary during the course of his oral evidence before the Committee 
explanined that the Ministry of Finance makes an assessment of the total amount of resources for 

development. The question of allocating these resources is the responsibility of Planning 
Commission which chalks oul the priority areas for which funds are to be allocated out of the 
total resources. The representative of the Ministry informed the Committee that during the 
discussion on the issue with PIB. the Secretary, Planning Commission and other officials felt that 
the Ministry of Steel should explore the private part icipation in liSCO modernisation. The 
Ministry of Steel decided the posstbility of private participation as SAIL was found incapable to 
undertake modernisation in view of its limited internal and extra budgetary resources. no 
budgetary support coming from Government and also its committed modernisation projects in 
plants at Durgapur, Bokaro, Rourkela etc. On being asked whether Government would consider 
extending tax benefits to SAIL if liSCO is merged with it, the Finance Secretary clarified that the 
SAIL never came forward for any type of concess ions nor has it ever sent any capital 
restructuring proposal, which would have been considered by his Ministry if received. He further 
clarified that his Ministry would have no objection if SAIL wants to internalise the losses of 
liSCO. Reacting to a question whether some budgetary support is possible for liSCO 
modernisation m view of improved economic situation and better foreign exchange reserves. the 
Finance Secretary informed the Committee that foreign reserves are meant for attracting 
investment in the country. According to him it is the Planning Commission which determmes the 
priority in that regard and in the present juncture the Planning Commission would have to cut 
plan expenditure of other sectors. Winding up his evidence the Finance Secretary maintained that 
if required his Ministry would have no objection to re-examine the whole issue of liSCO 
modernisation, which is a matter to be decided by SAIL. 
13. The Special Secretary, Planning Commission deposed before the Committee that priority 
in funds allocation for liSCO modernisation could not be materialised as SAIL failed to raise the 
expected financial resources despite of decontrol of steel and external borrowings and it was not 
possible to cut out plant expenditure from other sectors. According to him SAIL prepares tts 
annual as well as five year plans and for that guidelines have been issued by National 
Development Council and Parliament. The basic objective of the Planning Commission is to 
allocate the scarce resources available with Government to various competing demands of the 
national economy and it is not feasible to provide funds for liSCO modernisation because the 
kitty is limited and the same amoul)t could be used to provide basic needs for the people. 
14. Though the Statement of Objects and reasons declares that it ~viii be ensured that the 
assets of liSCO and the interest of workers are fully protected by the Committee finds that the 
provisions of the Bill are silent in that regard and there is no mentivn of workers at all. It boils 
down to the bare fact tha! the workers will be governed by the existing labour laws and in that 
eventuality the legal requirements can not be stopped. As such the Committee is of the opinion 
that the proposed amendments are against the Statement of Objects and Reasons and have not 
properly been drafted to be inconformity with the Statement of Objects and Reasons. There is 
every possibility of misuse of these proposed amendments in future. 
Conclusions: 
15. The Committee finds that the provisions of the Bill require to be specific in terms of 
ensuring that the workers' jobs are protected and adequate provisions should be made that no 
measures can be taken of retrenching them under any existing laws for the time bemg in force. 
As such the Bill needs to be re-drafted before it is introduced. The Committee feels that the 
Government has an inherent right to introduce a Bill in the Parliament, subject to leave being 
granted by a House. In a democratic polity the Government cannot be denied that right, though 
the Parliament in its wisdom can reject or pass the Bill depending on its merits. The workers' 
representatives have offered to participate in 50% equity which government may consider. 

15.1 The Committee finds that the terms and reference set out for the Committee of Experts 
were limited enough to restrain that Committee in recommeding concrete proposals for 
modernisation of liSCO. In fact Government should have ask.;!d the Committee to suggest all 
alternatives instead of concentrating on scrutiny of bids in the global tender for private 
participation. 
15.2 The Committee finds that at no stage SAIL has expresssed its mability to undertake the 
modernis?tion programme of liSCO and in fact SAIL has not been extended the required funds 
for the purpose during all these years despite its viable proposals submitted to the Government 
time and again and this fact has been corro oorated by the Financr Secretary in his oral evidence 
before the Committee. While clanfymg the point further the Spec ial Secretary of Planning 
Commission informed the Committee thai' tt is for the Ministry ·of Steel to readjust its priorities 
out of the total plan ouday. The Committee is thus not convinced with the Governments 
approach in rejecting the proposals made by SAIL itself towards the modernisation by not 
providmg the requisite budgetary support to SAIL out to its toral allocation made to it by 
Planning Commission by readjusting its priorities for liSCO. 
15.3 In v1ew of 1ts above mentioned observations, and also the fact that this is the ftrst time 
Government proposes to privatise a public sector steel company in the country, the Committee 
recommends that an indepth study of the modernisation proposals should be made again before 
reaching a final decision about the fate of the company. While doing so in inviting fresh offers al! 
the past offers may also be considered. The:·efore, even now, Government should work out a 
practicable formula through consesus. For this the management, workers and the Government 
should sit together and devise through a tripartite discussion some positive solutions to modernise 
the company The Committee had rccieved reservation on the technical competence or companies 
not having expenencL. in the making of steel through the open hearth furnace route. SAIL has 
full capabilities in this regurd and this needs to be explored in greater depth. The workers have 
3lso come forth with tremendous enthus1asm offering as high as 50% particip tion by them. The 
West Bengal Lcgi:-lattve Assembly has also passed a resolution lli1animou!.ly supporting and 
recommending that SAIL mu!.t take over the entire responsibilities and modernisation of liSCO. 
The possibility of the \llest Bengal Government takmg over liSCO should also be explored on 
the same terms and L~nditions. The Committee believes that, m brining the iegislation, in the 
presen: global scenar io ano the a·.,ailability ot substantial foreign moPe~ as also consider ing that 
the decision of not ronsidcnng the offer from a large multinational company and another large 
steel company in the private sector having the open hearth furance experience and more 
importantly 'IS mentioned above that this is the first attempt of the nation to privatise a public 
sector steel pla t, the Government should consider all these important facts in its perspective.

was not introduced m 1he Lok Sabha 1t is not being appended to this report.

CHAPTER-I

RECOMMENDATION
 
             The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Heavy Industry should take the matter with customer PSEs/Department for releasing of

COMMENTS
 
              Government have taken up the matter with the concerned Ministries for release  of  withheld  payments wherever necessary.  However, complaints have

RECOMMENDATION
 
            Richardson & Cruddas Ltd. is  one of the PSEs which has been functioning successfully after the  implementation of  revival package but  still the
Company is facing a major  problem  of excess manpower . Secondly due to the excess manpower they has been no wage   revision of the employees  for long as
a result of which the moral of the employees has touched its  nadir. 
 
           The Committee, therefore, recommends immediate sanction of requisite funds for  the implementation of Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS)  and wage-
revision of the employee as any delay would not be  in the interest of the Company.
 
COMMENTS
 
             Government have provided GOI counter guarantee to the tune of Rs.11 crores to R&C to raise funds through issue of bonds for implementation of VRS
in the Company. Apart from this, an amount of Rs.21.02 crores has been provided under VRS to R&C in order to reduce its manpower cost during the current
year. 
  RECOMMENDATION
 
          The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Government should sympathetically consider the grants for VRS to save the Byculla Unit.
 
COMMENTS
 
          As detailed above, Government have already provided funds for implementation of VRS to R&C. Out of the funds recently released by the Government,
around 333 employees have taken VRS from the Byculla Unit of the Company
                        RECOMMENDATION
                       
                                    The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Heavy Industry should initiate  the matter with the Ministry of Railways
and do needful for placing  the work-orders  on Richardsons & Cruddas Ltd. 
                 
         COMMENTS
 
                                    As the Byculla Unit of R&C owing to its poor performance over the years, has become unviable and  a drain on the overall profitability of
the company,  the management has  decided to introduce  VRS in the company.   As a result out  of the total strength of about  430, around 333 employees have  
opted for VRS.   With  the adoption of VRS by the remaining employees, the viability  of the company will improve.  The Department has also been taking up
with the Ministry of Railways from time to time  for placing of work orders on R&D.

In the stiff  competition posed by domestic  and overseas suppliers  Bharat Pumps and Compressors has been facing  challenges  from the private sector  due to

imposing stiff  terms and conditions   which the company is unable to meet  due to  obsolete plant & machinery and shortage of working capital.

Government have taken  up the matter with the concerned Ministries/Departments at the level of Minister (heavy Industries   and Public Enterprises) for

CHAPTER – II
RECOMMENDATION/OBSERVATION, WHICH THE COMMITTEE DOES    NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT’S
REPLIES
     RECOMMENDATION 
 
The Committee observed that BYNL as a holding company has not been able to assist its subsidiaries to come out of the wood. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that all the six subsidiaries of the BYNL should be merged into a single Company  so that the newly merged Company can pool together all the
resources of the subsidiaries and stand on a sound economic ground and this may help them in bidding for LSTK projects and by having effective control on its
Units act as the main agent for  securing  orders, rationalizing manpower, ensuring VRS grant from the  Government, etc. and eventually emerge as a pioneer to
the other Central /State  PSEs.
 
COMMENTS
 
BYNL was incorporated in 1986 as a wholly owned Company of Government of India. It started functioning w.e.f. 1.4.1987. Six subsidiaries namely, SHPV,
BPCL, B&R, R&C, TSL and TSPL came under its fold in April, 1987. This concept of holding company with subsidiaries under its fold came into existence
based on the recommendations of an expert Committee.
At present, the six subsidiaries under BYNL are operating in different areas of specialisation. Out of the six subsidiaries, three namely; BPCL, R&C and TSL are
sick and under reference to BIFR. Their revival plans sanctioned by BIFR are under review of BIFR and future of these companies will depend on the final
recommendations of BIFR. While three companies namely; BHPV, BPCL and TSPL have been identified for Joint Venture (JV) formation and action to convert
them into JV is already on. Once the exercise is complete, the status of these companies will undergo change. The recommendation to merge all the six
subsidiaries into a single company will bring into focus a set of problems with regard to inter-subsidiary seniority of the employees, different pay scales
applicable in Schedule 'A', 'B, and 'C' PSEs and other terms & conditions applicable to respective companies. It may lead to litigation by employees respective
Unions/Associations.
CHAPTER – III
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS IN RESPECT OF WHICH THE COMMITTEE HAS NOT ACCEPTED REPLIES OF THE
GOVERNMENT
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
           The first major problem, which warrants the attention of this Sub-Committee, is the delay in approval of the restructuring of the subsidiary companies of
BYNL .  It is felt that Department of Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industries  and Public Enterprises seems to have a very indifferent approach towards the
preparation, approval and implementation of the restructuring packages for these subsidiary companies .
 
         The Committee feels that any delay on the whole process involving the restructuring of a Company smacks of lack of commitment  on the part of the
Government . Therefore, the Committee recommends that the Department of Heavy Industry , Ministry of Heavy Industries  and Public Enterprises, should make
conscious  efforts to help these subsidiary companies by approval , timely preparation, and implementation of their restructuring- packages .
 
COMMENTS
 
Out of six subsidiary companies of BYNL group, three companies namely, BPCL, R&C and TSL are sick PSEs under reference to B1FR. The rehabilitation
schemes sanctioned by BIFR in respect of these PSEs are under implementation since 1995. However, these companies have not been able to match the
projections given  in the BIFR scheme despite grant of all reliefs & concessions given by the Government. During the year 1999, Government appointed M/s
CRISIL Advisory Services as Consultant to undertake diagnostic study to suggest ways & means for revival of these companies. Based on the reports of M/s
CRISIL, draft Cabinet Note envisaging package of financial assistance for TSL has been prepared and circulated to all concerned for their comments. After
receiving comments from the various Ministries/Departments, the Note will be placed before the Cabinet for its decision in the matter. As suggested by the
Consultant, a package of assistance in respect of BPCL is also under preparation and will be finalised and circulated to all concerned for comments and further
action will be taken in the matter.
 
The remaining three subsidiaries of the group namely, BHPV, B&R and TSPL  as well as BPCL have been identified by the Government for Joint Venture (JV)
formations. BHPV, BPCL and TSPL's cases have already been referred to Department of Disinvestment (DOD) which has been mandated to handle
disinvestment in Central PSES. Restructuring is to form part of the disinvestment JV  formation.  Restructuring proposal of B&R is under consideration of this
Department as a prelude to JV formation in due course.
 
COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATION
 
            The Committee expects that implementation of revival packages will lead to the revival of B.P.C.L. and T.S.L. The Committee, therefore, recommends
that  their restructuring proposal should be finalized at the earliest. The Committee also suggests that a similar revival package should be initiated by the
Department of Heavy Industry in respect of R&C. The Committee notes that B.H.P.V., B &R,  T.S.P.L. and B.P.C.L. have been  identified by the Govt. for Joint-
Venture formation. The Committee feels that financial restructuring would help these companies in improving their performance  and also enable them to be in a 
position to get commercial borrowings. It will also help in getting attractive prices from the bidders. The Committee, therefore, recommends that the financial
restructuring of these companies may be implemented at the earliest.
 
  RECOMMENDATION
 
            The issue of  timely payment of arrears and strategy to reduce  the employees of these subsidiary companies merit the Committee’s serious consideration

as it has a direct bearing on the well-being of thousands of employees.
            The Committee, therefore, recommends that arrears and statutory dues  should be paid  to the employees forthwith by earmarking separate funds for this
purpose . The Ministry merely becoming a helpless spectator  in the matter  by saying that the matter is being examined by a Group of Ministers does not end the
responsibility of the Administrative Ministry. The Ministry should own the responsibility in this regard and take up  the matter  seriously with the Government at
appropriate forum for the release of  funds for the payments of wage arrears, statutory dues, etc. by arranging some separate fund for the purpose, if necessary,  in
conjunction with other Ministries  whose  PSEs are also not able to pay  salaries to their employees.
 
COMMENTS
 
            Due to poor generation of internal resources, BPCL, R&C, TSL and TSPL have been defaulting in payment of statutory dues like gratuity, PF etc. This
Department has taken up the matter with Ministry of Finance for allocation of funds to meet the liabilities on account of wage arrears and statutory dues.
 
COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATION
 
            The Committee understands that the Department of Heavy Industry has been providing non-plan finds for the purpose which are not adequate. The
Committee, therefore, stresses the need for arranging special funds for this purpose.           
RECOMMENDATION
 
                       During the visit of the Committee to various subsidiaries companies it was found that there was not enough work order with these subsidiaries as a
result of  which  the entire  activities of  these subsidiary companies may come to a grinding halt at any moment.
 
           The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Heavy Industry, Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises, should   take up the
matter with the Union Cabinet and necessary instructions should be  issued for those customer-PSEs and Departments for placing adequate orders on these 
subsidiaries of  BYNL.
 
COMMENTS
 
           Government   has been taking up with the  concerned Ministries Departments/State Governments, the issue      of award of work orders on BYNL group of
companies. After the intervention of the Government, some of the subsidiaries have been able to secure sufficient orders from their clients.
 
COMMITTEE’S OBSERVATION
 
            Even after the intervention  of  the Government, subsidiaries such as TSPL, B&R, BPCL and R&C are not getting sufficient work orders from the Central
and State Governments PSEs and Agencies. The Committee would like to know the details of work orders reserved for the BYN Companies. The Committee
recommends that Department Heavy Industry  should persuade the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas for placement of part of work-orders for fabricated
equipments and pumps and  compressors on nomination basis on BHPV and BPC respectively from the refineries coming up  in the country. Similarly there
should be reservation of certain percentage of orders for R&C from the Railways. The Committee also recommends that Department  of Heavy Industry should
take up the matter with NHPC, NHDC and State Governments for placement of work-orders on TSPL  from the Hydro Power Projects coming up in the country
and irrigation projects coming up in the various States respectively.
  .
RECOMMENDATION
 
          Many subsidiaries are having excess manpower that has proved a handicap to function in the post liberalization era . Although planned rationalization of

and Roof Company has to perforce maintain the establishment at Nepal since they cannot abandon the project unless the terminals are formally taken over by

      CHAPTER – I 
  
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE 
GOVERNMENT 
  
  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
          Last but not the least, under the present scen ario of stiff competition from private and global companies, th e
DPE should strengthen the MoU system specially where is sues involving inter-ministerial/ inter PSU co-ordinatio n
are concerned. The DPE should play a pro-active role in making the PSUs competitive and strengthening them fo r
sustained growth. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
            Efforts are made during the MOU negotiat ion meetings to achieve the inter-ministerial and inter-PSU 
coordination. The incorporation of PSU-s pecific efficiency parameters in the MOUs is an attempt to improve the 
profitability and competitive strength of the PSUs. Theref ore, the MOU system already plays, an active role in 
strengthening the PSEs to become more competitive. These efforts will be further continued.  
  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The MoU system has undeniably made a positive contribu tion to improve the performance of the PSEs.  The 
management of PSEs were appreciative of the fact that the MoU system has, for the first time brought about clarity o f 
the goals to be achieved on the basis of precise targets laid down in the MoU ensuring accountability on an objective 
basis.  They were also enthusiastic of the larger delegati on of powers available to the MoU signing Companies.  The 
managements of the PSEs could act freely to a great extent with clear-cut objec tives and goals.  Especially in thei r 
day-to-day operations, the interference by the Ministries had reduced to a considerable extent. This has provided an 
opportunity to the managements to take quick decisions and furthermore, evaluation of their performance is now 
being done in a very objective and transparent basis. 
  
  
COMMENTS 
  
The observations of the Standing Committee on the work ing of the MOU system are taken note of and efforts 
will be made to further strengthen it.  
  
   
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee also feels that through the MoU system, an effort has been made to synthesise different 
objectives.  Under the MoU system the parameters selected  as performance indicators ar e a good mix of financial, 
dynamic and efficiency indicators.  Thus, it is not only the financial parameters  which are given importance but other 
dynamic and efficiency parameters  whic h are very essential for the future growth of the PSEs, and which are also 
incorporated as performance indicators.  Thus, under the present system an attemp t has been made to strike a balance 
between financial and non-financial parameters.  The Comm ittee is of the firm view that the MoU system has 
produced reasonable results as it is unders tood that during the negotiation meetings an effort is made to set targets, 
which represent an improvement over the level of performance  in the previous year, and the system has significantly 
contributed to a progressive increase in the performance of PSEs.  The Committee, ther efore, recommends that the 
MoU system should continue on a long-term basis. 
  
COMMENTS

            The observations of the Standing Committee on the importance of MOU system has been taken note of and it 
has been decided to continue the system on a long term basis.         
   
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
Recently, the Public Sector Enterprises have been expos ed to domestic and international competition.  Most 
of them were operating in a totally protective environmen t.  With the policy of liberalisation and globalisation, the 
PSEs have to compete in the market for obtaining orders bot h in products and services.  For a PSE to be competitive 
it is essential to have an edge over its competitors, both in cost and quality.  In such a situation, the Committee feels 
that  up gradation of technology including modernisation, up gradation of skills of em ployees and rationalisation o f 
manpower etc. are key factors to generate necessary comp etitive strength to PSEs.  The Committee, therefore, 
recommends that the MoU system should be used as an effective instrument to bring about the change in the working 
environment of the PSEs by introducing specific strategies through it to make them more competitive. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
            To a large extent technology upgradati on, modernisation, upgradation of skills of employees and 
rationalisation of manpower etc. generally form part of the dynamic parameters, which are incorporated in the MOUs. 
However, more emphasis will be laid on these issues while  issuing the guidelines for formulation of draft MOUs fo r 
next year.  
  
   
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
On the question of reduction of budgetary support to Depa rtment of Public Enterprises and its consequent 
winding up in pursuance of recommendation of Expenditure  Reforms Commission (EFC), it has not considered the 
essentially vital role played by the  Department of P ublic Enterprises in making the Memoranda of Understanding 
which the Government of India enters with its Public Sector  Units on the annual basis.  The Department is merely not 
facilitating but enabling the MoU to be an important tool for performance assessment mutates mutandis to that o f 
Profit Center Concepts of large Conglomerates in devel oped countries.  The MoU is an  effective and objective tool 
today only because of it being facilitate d by a non-stakeholder that is Department  of Public Enterprises.  Hence, the 
Committee strongly feels that the Department of  Public Enterprises should be strengthened with budgetary support.   
  
COMMENTS 
  
The   objective of MOU system was to improve the performance of PSEs  and to intruduce a mechanism to 
evaluate the performance of the managements in an objective and transparent manner and it was in this interest, the 
job of implementing the MOU system was entrusted to a nodal Department. The need to strengthen the Department 
with budgetary support is taken note of and will be reviewed while formulating the budget proposals. 
  
   
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee observes that the strength of the MoU system is that the targets are finalised and the 
performance of the PSE is evaluated in an objective and transparent manner that is ensured by the DPE and ATF.  
Thus, in order to maintain and further instil objectivity, th e Committee feels that DPE should play a more active role 
in the process and the MoU Division should be strengthene d so that they can carry out bench marking studies, 
performance related studies and other associated work so that the targets given to the PSEs are more realistic. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
               The MOU Division has the benefit of getting the advice of the ATF which is a body of experts an d
academicians eminent in their respective fields. Functi ons like conduction benchmark studies, performance relate d
studies can be sourced out to prominent professional bodi es. The need for strengthening MOU Division and playing a
more active role in the process has been take note of.

RECOMMENDATION 
  
             The Committee is, however, constrained to note that the MoU Division of the Department of  Public 
Enterprises has been proposed to be abolished.  The Secret ary, Ministry of Heavy Indus try and Public Enterprises, 
during the course of his oral evidence before the Committee in connection with the Demands for Grants, informed the 
Committee that the Expenditure Reforms Commission has recommended that the Department of Public Enterprises 
may be down-sized .  It was proposed that  the  MoU Syst em  may be transferred to the respective Administrative
Ministries of the concerned PSEs. The Committee, however, does not agree with this.   The Committee feels that the 
Department of Public Enterprises provides a neutral forum for finalising MoUs  which is essential to make it an 
objective systems.  It is also ensured that the entire MoU ex ercise is carried out in an objective, transparent and broad 
based manner.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that instead of transferring the MoU System to the concerned 
Administrative Departments, it may be retained with the De partment of Public Enterprise s. In fact the MoU Division 
needs to be further strengthened for an effective implementation of the MoU System.  
  
COMMENTS 
  
In order to ensure the objectivity of the system the job of implementing the MOU system was entrusted to a 
nodal Department, if the task of  preparing/finalising the MOUs is left to the respective concerned Administrative 
Ministries such a situation is bound to defeat the very purpose of having the MOU system. It has accordingly been 
decided not to transfer the MOU related work to the Admini strative Ministries and it will continue to the with DPE 
whose nodal and neutral status will be maintained. As regards the need for strengthening the MOU Division the 
recommendation of the Committee has been noted.  
  
CHAPTER-II 
  
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATION WHICH THE COMMITTEE  
 DOES NOT DESIRE TO PURSUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENTS’ REPLIES  
  
  
  
RECOMMENDATION 
  
The Committee is constrained to note that the MoU prep aration has generally been an annual target setting 
exercise.  The Committee feels that the MoU system should focus on strategic issues rather than be a mere annual 
target setting exercise.  For that purpose the Administ rative Ministries should provi de adequate input/support to 
enable PSEs to develop future strategies in association wi th the Ministries.  The parameters under the MoU need to 
be devised depending upon the strategy for its future growth in the particular area of its operations.  The performance 
of the PSEs needs to be reviewed on the basis of parameters so devised.  This would give a clear picture as to how a 
particular PSE has been able to make its products/services  cost effective and how they compare with their counte r 
parts in the private sector.  Such an approach would certa inly make the PSEs not only competitive but also provide an 
opportunity to become global players.  Therefore, the Committee suggests that the approach under the MoU system 
needs to be reviewed in line with the existing competitive economic environment. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
The Ad-hoc Task Force is already seized of this issue and during the MOU ne gotiation meetings, great 
importance is attached to the strategic issues. Further efforts in this regard will continue to bring to the notice of the 
PSEs and Administrative Ministries, the crucial importance of the strategi c issues and impressing upon them to 
develop appropriate strategies for improvement of the performance of the PSEs.  
  
   
RECOMMENDATION

It is felt that setting  up of an Export Promotion Cell for CPSUs in DPE may cut across the legitimate

the front end, it can invite, in the fi rst instance, other concerned telecom PSUs to be consortium partners, on the basis

            The Committee desires that the DPE should c ontinuously review the progress made in this regard and monito r

RECOMMENDATION 
  
There have been persistent efforts by various Depart ments with the Finance Ministry to correct the duty 
structure.  With the liberalisation, the duties on the finished goods have come down faster than the duties on the raw 
materials in electronic and information technology.  If the duty structure is not corrected , the people will find import

            The Committee is of the view that rationa lisation of the duty structure is  of utmost importance to mak e

RECOMMENDATION 
  
Though the parameters such as preparation and implem entation of corporate plan  and devising a strategic 
plan or vision plan, etc. are being me ntioned in the MoU documents, the targets set in the MoUs do not often 
correspond to the corporate vision/plans drawn up by the PSEs.  The Committee, therefore, stresses that there should 
be a better linkage between the corporate plans of the PSEs and the MoUs.  
  
COMMENTS 
  
            Most of the PSEs have now formulated co rporate plans, as this has been impressed upon them during the 
MOU negotiation meetings. This recommendation of  the Standing Committee has been noted and the 
PSEs/Administrative Ministries  will be requested through the guidelines that are proposed to be issued for the 
formulation of MOUs for the next year to try and establish the necessary linkages between the corporate plans and the 
MOU targets.  
  
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATIONS  
  
            DPE  may ensure implementation of this by a ll Ministries. This is necessary because if the targets of MOUs 
do not correspond with corporate vision/plans, the MOUs preparation  will be a futile exercise.   
  
   
RECOMMENDATION 
  
As PSEs have to operate in a free market, they cannot continue to depend upon Government’s assistance on 
matters such as obtaining orders, etc.  In the present situ ation, negotiating for orders is  a managerial function and, 
therefore, the Government’s  intervention should be very sel ective, if at all.  For inst ance, a number of the PSEs are 
working in the same area but they are under the control of different administrative minist ries.  In some cases, these 
PSEs operate as competitors to each other.  Similarly, PSEs are also involved in research and development projects 
and some of the PSEs are spending quite a significant  MoU units  on R&D activities.  Unfortunately, these PSEs are 
working in isolation and there is no coordination to provide synergy in R& D, marketing, etc. to enhance thei r 
competitive edge over their counter partners in the private sectors.  Since these PSEs are functioning in watertight 
compartments, they are not able to reap the maximum benefits of their investments on R&D and up gradation o f 
technology.  Separate and isolated efforts on the part of the PSEs in such areas only result in addition to their costs.  
Therefore, there is tremendous scope in bringing together  PSEs operating in the same discipline, but under different 
Ministries, to optimise inve stments in marketing, R&D etc. in a collect ive and coordinated manner.  The Committee, 
therefore, feels that the Department of Public Enterp rises operating through the MoU system appears to be an 
appropriate forum where the issues involving inter-ministries /inter-PSEs coordination can be taken up more 
effectively and DPE as a nodal Department should play a mo re pro-active role in making the PSEs competitive and 
strengthening them for sustained growth. 
  
COMMENTS 
  
            The possibility of such synergy exists  particularly in the area of R&D, Technology up gradation and 
marketing. Sub optimal investment by individual PSEs often does not generate  productive results. On the other hand, 
a collaborative effort in the field of R&D and marketing by pooling the resources of different enterprises can produce 
useful results. In the MOU negotiation meetings, it is generally attempted to bring together PSEs in the same 
discipline and explore such possibilities.

REPORT
         The Sixty Second Report of the Committee deals with the Action Taken by the Government on the Recommendations contained in its 48th
Report of the Department Related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Industry on the Demands For Grants 2000-2001 pertaining to the
Department of Public Enterprises  which was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of Lok Sabha on  the 14th  May, 2001.
 
2.         Action Taken Notes have been received from the Government in respect of the recommendations contained in the Report. They have been
categorized as follows:
             
 (i)        Recommendations/Observations, which have been accepted by the Government:- Para  6.14;  6.15;  6.16;  6.17;  6.18 and 6.19.   ( Chapter -
I).
 
 (ii)       Recommendation/Observation which the Committee does not desire to pursue in view of the government’s replies: - Para  2.8;  4.3 and 4.5 .
   (Chapter - II).
 
 (iii)      Recommendations/Observations in respect of which the Committee has not accepted replies of the Government: - Para 2.5;  3.5;  3.9;  4.5; 
5.4;  5.6;  5.7 and 5.8. (Chapter - III).
 
 (iv)      Recommendations/Observations in respect of which final replies of the Government have not been received: -NIL. (Chapter – IV).
           
  (v)      Observations/Recommendations at a Glance . (Chapter – V).
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY      THE GOVERNMENT
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
After hearing the Secretary, Department of Public Enterprises, the Committee expressed its unhappiness that the Expenditure Reforms Commission
has recommended that the task of preparing MoUs can be left as well to the concerned administrative Ministries.  The Committee feels that the said
Commission in an anxiety to reduce the Government expenditure undermined the role of a nodal agency, i.e., Department of Public Enterprises
without evaluating its performance over the years.
COMMENTS
 
The recommendations of the Committee were kept in view while reviewing the role and functions of DPE in the context of the recommendations
made by the ERC and it has been decided that the work relating to MOU can not be transferred to the Administrative Ministries and should continue
to be performed by the DPE in the interest of maintaining objectivity and credibility of the system apart from ensuring transparency and
accountability.
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee is also of the view that a unified central agency to implement the MoU system is certainly more cost effective rather than
having separate MoU Units in all the Administrative Ministries.  Similarly, pooling expertise for all the Ministries from the same ATF as is being
done at present by the Department of Public Enterprises is also cost effective.
 
COMMENTS
 
The recommendations of the Committee have been kept in view and it has been decided to continue with the present arrangement of implementing
the MOU System by the nodal Department namely, DPE rather than leaving the task of preparing MOUs to the concerned Administrative Ministries
as recommended by the ERC.  The present system of implementing MoU System through a unified central agency like DPE is not only cost-
effective but also imparts objectivity and credibility to the system.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee further feels that the Department of Public Enterprises provides a neutral forum for finalizing the MoUs, which is essential
to make it an objective system, and it should not be abolished.
 
COMMENTS
 
Government agrees with the view of the Committee that a neutral forum like the Department of Public Enterprises is necessary for finalizing MOUs
to make it an objective system. Government has no intention to dilute its nodal and neutral status as at present.
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee is also of the firm view that the object of signing MoUs would not be achieved in the absence of an over-seeing agency, i.e.
Department of Public Enterprises.
 

62nd Report

COMMENTS
 
The Government agrees with the views of the Committee. DPE’s status as a nodal and neutral over-seeing agency will continue.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the proposal of abolishing MoU Division may be shelved.  As the country is now on
the threshold of making PSEs more vibrant, productive and efficient, it is very essential that the MoU Division should be further strengthened
instead of being abolished.  Strengthening of MoU Division would go a long way in making PSEs profitable and responsive to competitiveness.
 
COMMENTS
 
The Government accepts the recommendations of the Committee. There is no proposal to abolish the MOU Division. As regards strengthening this
Division, position is reviewed from time to time  and appropriate action  taken wherever necessary.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, therefore, again recommends that the Department of Public Enterprises should be strengthened so as to make it more
responsive.
 
COMMENTS
 
The recommendations of the Committee have been noted. Periodical review of the organizational structure of DPE is being conducted and
whenever necessary, action is being taken to strengthen the Department to make it more responsive.
CHAPTER-II
 
THE COMMITTEE DOES  NOT DESIRE TO PURUE IN VIEW OF THE GOVERNMENT' S REPLIES
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The committee is of the view that the present staff strength numbering about 136 of the Department of Public Enterprises needs to be
increased in view of the wide roles and functions being undertaken by the Department.  The Department needs to be strengthened.
 
COMMENTS
 
In the context of the recommendations of the Expenditure Reforms Commission (ERC), the role and functions of the Department were reviewed and
15 posts at various levels were abolished. The above recommendation  has been noted and the staff strength will be reviewed as per needs and due
strengthening and rationalisation will be done  where required.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The existing rate of Rs.9000 per head for non-recurring expenses towards infrastructure, office equipments, preparatory works, training
expenses, follow-up services, etc. of nodal agency, may prove insufficient.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the existing rate of Rs.9000
per head may be reviewed.  If necessary,  the allocation may be increased.
 
COMMENTS
 
This is the first year of implementation of  the Training programme  by the Department of Public Enterprises. The advice of the Committee is being
noted and while reviewing  the working of the scheme, the per head cost along with other aspects of the scheme would  be considered.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee feels that the Department of Public Enterprises is over burdened after being assigned the tasks of counselling, retraining and
redeployment of rationalized employees of Central PSEs.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Department of Public Enterprises should
involve/appoint new technocrats, Research Officers, skilled workers etc.
COMMENTS
 
The recommendation of the Committee has been noted. The position with regard to implementation of the scheme would be reviewed periodically,
when the manpower requirement could also be reviewed.
 
                CHAPTER-III
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS WHICH HAVE  NOT  BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT

62nd Report

RECOMMENDATION
 
            Since substantial new tasks have been assigned to the Department of Public Enterprises, the allocation of Rs.10.86 crores made for the year
2001-2002 does not appear to be sufficient.  The Committee, therefore, recommends that the allocation made to the department by the Government
may be reviewed in the supplementary demands for grants.
 
COMMENTS
 
As far as the work relating to retraining and redeployment of rationalized employees of PSEs is concerned, this is the first year of implementation of
the Training Programme by the Department of Public Enterprises. The recommendation of the Committee is being noted and will be kept in view
while reviewing the Scheme.
 
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATION
           
The Committee is of the view that the work relating to retraining and redeployment of rationalised employees of central PSEs recently assigned to
the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) is an important matter in the present context, which needs to be reviewed and monitored periodically.
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, however, would like to know how far such an enlarged Board of Directors consisting of official/non-officials/part time
Directors has produced the desired results.  The Committee feels that the Department of Public Enterprises should undertake a study in the matter.
 
COMMENTS
 
While granting enhanced autonomy and authority under Navratna and Miniratna, one of the preconditions was that Boards of these Navratna and
Miniratna CPSUs should be professionalised by inducting of non-official part-time Directors through Search Committee. Accordingly the exercise
for professionalisation of Boards in case of existing 11 Navratna CPSUs was completed in April, 1999.  In case of Miniratna, Board of Directors of
17 CPSUs out of 46 have been restructured by co-opting part-time professional Directors. It may be mentioned that the Boards are not enlarged, but
only vacant positions have been filled.
A study was carried out in consultation with all the 11 navratna PSUs and those Miniratna PSUs, where non-official part-time Directors have been
inducted. It is revealed that the Boards have exercised the enhanced powers to a large extent. The induction of non-official Directors has helped in
professionalising the Boards of these PSUs and also to set up various sub-committees like Audit Committee. The non-official Directors with their
rich experience and expertise in various areas like management, administration, finance, marketing, technology, etc. have contributed substantially
in the Board deliberations. Thus the study has revealed that the by and large induction of non-official professional Directors has produced the
desired results.
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATION
 
            The Committee feels that autonomy of  PSUs should not be limited by Govt. control and such Companies should be fully Board-managed
Companies in all matters. In an environment of stiff competition in the post liberalisation era, the PSUs can not function effectively without
sufficient freedom of operation and level playing field. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Boards of Directors of at least MOU-signing
Companies should be given sufficient powers to enable them to take quick decisions in their business related  matters, by reviewing the extent of the
current powers relating to limit on investment, access to capital market, repayment of foreign loans, foreign visits  by Boards of Directors for their
business position,  forming of joint ventures, exploring foreign markets etc. 
 
            The Committee feels that many PSUs remain headless without any CMD for a long time. This cripples the functioning of the PSUs.
Therefore, as and when any PSU is without CMD for three months, immediate action should be taken to appoint CMD. The Committee understands
that the appointments of CMDs of Central  PSUs is done by Public Enterprises Selection Board. Earlier this Board was under the Department of
Public Enterprises which is presently being controlled by the Ministry of Personnel & Training . The Committee, therefore, recommends that this
Board may be shifted from the purview of  the Ministry of Personnel & Training  to the Department of Public Enterprises for an effective 
monitoring  of  the functioning of the Central PSUs.
 
            Smaller PSUs at micro level are facing lot of challenges of the competition. The best way to make PSUs viable is to merge the related PSUs
so that the competition can be effectively faced. For this Government  may appoint a Committee to look into the issue of merger.
 
            The Committee further observes that only 108 PSUs out of 240 PSUs have signed the MoU system  with their Administrative
Ministries/Departments. The Committee stresses that all profit making PSUs should be brought under the ambit of the MoU system.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee, however, feels that the Department of Public Enterprises should review the performance of such companies in order to
know whether such companies are maintaining the status for which they were awarded such elevated positions.  The Committee feels that the
procedure to accord the Navratna status is a tardy procedure which needs to be revised by the Government.  Secondly, the responsibility of
accordance of the status of Miniratna, presently being held by the respective administrative ministries themselves to the concerned PSE, must be
transferred to the Search Committee under the Department of Public Enterprises.

COMMENTS
 
In May, 2001 the Government  issued guidelines for review of performance of Navratna and Miniratna Enterprises and for divest/grant of Navratna
and Miniratna status as the case may be which covers the points raised by the Committee.  These guidelines include:
 
Apex Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary in the case of Navratna enterprises and Inter-Ministerial Committee headed by the Secretary,
Department of Public Enterprises in the case of Miniratna enterprises would regularly review the performance of such companies.
A comprehensive review would be undertaken every three years by the above mentioned respective Committees with regard to maintenance of the
Navratna/Miniratna status.  The Apex Committee would lay down the format for such a review.
The Apex Committee would also review the operations of Navratna/Miniratna schemes every three years and would make recommendations in
regard to further delegation of autonomy to these enterprises
The recommendations of the Apex Committee, if any, for divestment of the Navratna status would be put up to the Minister(Heavy Industries and
Public Enterprises) for approval through the Minister in-charge of the administrative Ministry concerned.  In case of any disagreement, the matter
would be put up to the cabinet.
The recommendations of the divestment of Miniratna status would be dealt with by concerned administrative Ministry only.
 
The recommendations for accordance of Navratna status to a CPSU would, ordinarily, not be placed before the Cabinet.  Based on the
recommendations of the Apex Committee these would be placed before the Minister for Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises for taking a final
decision.  But as in (iv) above, in case of disagreement, the matter would be put up to the Cabinet.
 
This guideline has set in place separate Committee to review the performance of Navaratna and Miniratna PSEs. The periodicity of the review will
be every 3 years. It has also laid down the procedure for according Navaratna Status.
 
The recommendation of assigning the task of accordance of the status of Miniratnas to the Search Committee under DPE has been noted and will be
kept in view at the time of reviewing of the existing mechanism.
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATION
 
            The Committee desires that an early decision may be taken regarding assigning the tasks of accordance of the status of Miniratnas to the
Search Committee under DPE. The Committee reiterates its earlier recommendation that the procedure to accord Navaratna status may be revised
and simplified.
RECOMMENDATION  (5.4)
 
            The Committee recommends that the Purchase Preference Policy should be extended for another 3 years, i.e., upto 31.3.2004
 
COMMENTS
 
Recommendation of the Committee has been noted and the position will be reviewed at appropriate time.
           
RECOMMENDATION ( 5.6 )
 
            The Committee is very much concerned to note that certain Central PSEs/Central Govt. Agencies are not including the Purchase Preference
clause in their Notice Inviting Tender(NIT) depriving the other Central PSEs to avail the benefit of the Government Policy.  This non-cooperative
attitude of some of the PSEs does not go well with the overall policy of the government to improve the health of PSEs.  The highlights indicated by
the Minister would remain only highlights without a major shift in their health status.  If there has to be a major reversal in the health condition of
the PSEs, all the PSEs  need to have mutual cooperation.  Purchase Preference Policy is one such grey area which, if followed scrupulously by all
the PSUs, would improve the performance of all the ailing PSEs.
 
COMMENTS
 
Govt. have noted the recommendations of the Committee.
 
RECOMMENDATION  (5.7)
 
            The Committee, therefore, recommends that all the Administrative Ministries/Government Departments should issue the instructions to the
PSEs under their jurisdiction to comply with the policy of the Government on Purchase Preference.
COMMENTS
 
DPE  issues general guidelines on various issues pertaining to CPSUs.  It is for the concerned Administrative Ministry/Department to ensure that the
guidelines issued by the Government including DPE are implemented by the PSUs.  The recommendations of the Committee will be circulated to

RECOMMENDATION  (5.8)
 
The Committee also recommends that the Department of Public Enterprises should ensure and monitor the compliance of the Purchase Preference
Policy.  In this regard all Public Sector Enterprises may be asked to submit documents of NIT to the Department of Public Enterprises for regular

compliance.
 
COMMENTS
 
Government have noted the recommendation of the Committee and would take appropriate action at the time of review of the policy
 
COMMITTEE'S OBSERVATIONS ON THE PURCHASE PREFERENCE POLICY ------  ( 5.4,  5.6,  5.7 & 5.8 )
 
(1-5.4)             In this connection, the Sub-Committee-III for the Ministry of Heavy Industries & Public Enterprises took up this matter for
consideration and held discussions with the Secretary, the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises.
 
The Secretary observed that if the PSEs were to be efficient, the crutches were to be removed. The Secretary informed that this policy provided
Purchase Preference in supply of goods and services to the government departments and other PSEs if the price quoted by the supplying PSE was
within 10% of the lowest valid bid price, other things being equal.  The policy was extended up to 31.3.02.  He pointed out that 51 PSUs took
advantage of the policy and 22 PSUs awarded the contracts under the policy.  There had been cases where Purchase Preference clause was not
included in the Notice Inviting Tenders (NIT).  The Administrative Ministries/Departments had been told to ensure that the guidelines issued by the
Government including D/o Public Enterprises were implemented by the PSEs.  He observed that there was slackness in following the guidelines and
it became difficult to correct action at a later stage wherever a violation of the guidelines took place.
 
            The Sub-Committee also held discussions with the CMDs of  many CPSUs and most of them have agreed that this policy should be
extended beyond 31.3.3002 and were also of the view that the policy should be strictly complied with by all PSUs.
 
            The Committee is  of the firm view that in the interest of the Nation and well being of the PSEs, the Purchase Preference Policy must
continue. It may be extended beyond 31
st April, 2002 at least for two more years.

RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS AT A GLANCE
           
The Committee is of the opinion that the work relating to retraining and redeployment of rationalised employees of central PSEs recently assigned
to the Department of Public Enterprises (DPE) is an important matter in the present context, which needs to be reviewed and monitored periodically.
( 2.5)
 
The Committee feels that autonomy of  PSUs should not be limited by Govt. control and such Companies should be fully Board-managed
Companies in all matters. In an environment of stiff competition in the post liberalisation era, the PSUs can not function effectively without
sufficient freedom of operation and level playing field. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Boards of Directors of at least MOU-signing
Companies should be given sufficient powers to enable them to take quick decisions in their business related  matters, by reviewing the extent of the
current powers relating to limit on investment, access to capital market, repayment of foreign loans, foreign visits  by Boards of Directors for their
business position,  forming of joint ventures, exploring foreign markets etc. 
 
            The Committee feels that many PSUs remain headless without any CMD for a long time. This cripples the functioning of the PSUs.
Therefore, as and when any PSU is without CMD for three months, immediate action should be taken to appoint CMD. The Committee understands
that the appointments of CMDs of Central  PSUs is done by Public Enterprises Selection Board. Earlier this Board was under the Department of
Public Enterprises which is presently being controlled by the Ministry of Personnel & Training . The Committee, therefore,  recommends that this
Board may be shifted from the purview of  the Ministry of Personnel Training  to the Department of Public Enterprises for an effective monitoring
of  the functioning of the Central PSUs.

           CHAPTER I
 
 
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERVATIONS, WHICH HAVE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
 
 
 
ROLE OF MINISTRY OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES AND AGRO &
RURAL INDUSTRIES IN THE POST LIBERALISATION ERA
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            Ministry’s role at this juncture becomes of paramount importance as it has to evolve mechanisms/directives/guidelines,
which will go a long way in shaping the course of things in future.  In view of these threats, safeguarding the interests of
indigenous industry is the major responsibility of the Ministry while formulating policies.  Government should provide level
playing field for the small scale industry to meet the challenges of stiff competition from global players.
 
COMMENTS
 
            To strengthen the small scale sector and  enhance its competitiveness, both domestically and globally, a comprehensive
policy package was announced on 30
th August, 2000 which inter-alia includes enhancement of excise exemption limit to Rs.1
crore, credit linked capital subsidy of 12% for technology up gradation, increase in investment limit in respect of industry related
service and business enterprises to Rs.10 lakh, enhancement of limit of collateral free composite loans from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.25
lakh, extension of  Integrated Infrastructure Development (IID) scheme to all areas, enhancement of limit of funding under
National Equity Fund Scheme of SIDBI from Rs.25 lakh to Rs. 50 lakh with 30% of the fund   earmarked for tiny sector, the
enhancement in eligibility limit under Credit Guarantee Scheme from Rs.10 lakh to Rs.25 lakh, the ongoing scheme of grant of
Rs.75,000 to each small scale enterprise for obtaining ISO 9000 Certification to be continued till the end of 10
th Plan, assistance of
one time capital grant of 50% on reimbursement basis to SSI associations etc.  
 
            The implementation of this policy package has been a focus area for the Ministry, 29 action points emerged out of this
package - follow up action has been completed in respect of 26 points.  This will go a long way in supporting SSIs.
 
            To enable hi-tech and export oriented industries in small scale sector, to have technology and quality upgradation and to be
able to have level playing field in the international market, Government de-reserved readymade garments.  The de-reservation of
toys and leather goods has also been effected recently.  The draft notification for enhancement of investment limit in respect of
hand tools and knitwears is laid before the Parliament and the final notification is expected shortly.
 
RECOMMENDATION
 
            The Committee has been given to understand that the competitive fervor unleashed by the liberalization process has led to a
paradigm shift in the nature of manufacturing activity in the country.  In such a scenario it has become imperative that the policy of
protection for small-scale sector should pave its way to a more proactive approach of helping such units to enhance their
competitiveness in a market driven economy.  If small and tiny enterprises have to compete in globalised environment they now
require an enabling and responsive environment, which provides adequate and timely credit and pragmatic institutional,
technological and infrastructural support.  The Committee hopes that the above proposals announced in the budget would mitigate
the hardships faced by the SSI Sector. The Government should, however, not feel complacent about this.
 
 
COMMENTS
 
            The Government is keeping constant watch on the changing environment. To ensure effective implementation of the
comprehensive policy package, there is a Policy Implementation Committee under the Chairmanship of AS & DC (SSI) and as
detailed above, action has already been completed in respect of 26 out of 29 points.  The Study Group on Development of Small
Scale Enterprises (Dr. S.P. Gupta Committee) has also submitted its final report, recommendations of which are under final
consideration of the Government.  The Working Group on SSI for the Tenth Plan is also looking into these issues particularly,
credit, technology, marketing and infrastructural support which could be provided to this sector.
